definition_zh: 收割；收获；获得（报酬、回报）；遭受（后果）
definition_en: to cut and gather a crop, or to get something such as a result, reward, or consequence
core_image: 镰刀贴着地面一挥，成排麦秆倒在农人身后
scene: 麦子熟了，农人一整天弯着腰挥镰割麦，身后留下一捆捆金黄。All day the farmer bent over his sickle and reaped the golden wheat.
sceneCN: 这里 reap 是「收割」（第 1 个义项：用镰刀割下并收拢庄稼）；句意：农人一整天弯腰挥镰，收割金黄的麦子。

pos.zh: 收割；收获
获得；得到（回报）；遭受（报应、后果）

derivatives.zh: 由 reap 加 -er 构成，指「收割者；收割机」；大写 Reaper 常指死神
由 reap 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「收割；收获」
与 reap 意义最接近的名词，义为「收割；收获」
收割用的镰刀，是 reap 这一动作最典型的工具

senses.title: To cut and gather a crop
senses.definition: to cut and gather grain or fruit from the fields
senses.definitionCN: 把田里的谷物或果实割下并收拢
senses.example: Farmers reap wheat at the end of summer.
senses.exampleCN: 农人在夏天末尾收割小麦。
senses.why: The old English word means to cut the stalks with a sickle, so reap names the cutting all along.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词就是「用镰刀割秆」，所以 reap 从头到尾都带着「割」的动作。

senses.title: To gather the yield
senses.definition: to bring in the produce of land or a harvestable resource
senses.definitionCN: 把地上的产物或可采集的资源收进家中
senses.example: The village reaps honey from wild hives each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 村民每年秋天从野蜂巢里采蜜。
senses.why: Cutting is only the first half of the work; the same word covers the gathering that follows.
senses.whyCN: 割只是前半件事，收拢则是后半件；同一个词把两步都包了下来。

senses.title: To gain as a result of effort
senses.definition: to get something good such as a reward, profit, or benefit from what one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因为做过的事而得到报酬、利润、好处之类的东西
senses.example: The company is reaping profits from its early investment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司正从早期的投资中获得利润。
senses.why: Fields give fruit only after long work, so the image moves from crops to any reward that follows effort.
senses.whyCN: 田地只有在长久劳动之后才给出果实，于是这个意象从作物移到了努力之后的一切回报。

senses.title: To suffer what is sown
senses.definition: to experience a bad result that is the natural consequence of earlier behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 经历因先前行为而必然出现的坏结果
senses.example: Industries that ignored warnings are now reaping the consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 当年无视警告的行业现在正在承受后果。
senses.why: The same harvest can be bitter as well as sweet, so reap takes on the sense of eating ones own crop.
senses.whyCN: 同一次收割既可能甘甜也可能苦涩，于是 reap 也带了「吃自己种下的果子」之意。

senses.title: To take something by force
senses.definition: in older and literary use, to seize quickly or to kill, as in the grim phrase the reaper
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文学用法里指迅速夺取或杀死，如「死神」的说法
senses.example: In the old tale the reaper took the whole household one winter.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个老故事里，一个冬天就把整户人家带走了。
senses.why: Harvest cuts everything standing in the field at once, so death was pictured as the one who cuts.
senses.whyCN: 收割把田里直立的东西一并割倒，于是死亡被画成「那个挥刀的人」。

intro.en: Reap is a native English word from Old English ripan, to cut grain, with close relatives in Dutch and Icelandic.
intro.cn: reap 是英语本土词，来自古英语 ripan（割谷物），在荷兰语与冰岛语里有亲近的同源词。

items.en: The reconstructed root ripanan is usually understood as grasping a handful of stalks in order to cut them.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 ripanan 的意思是「抓住一把秆子把它割下」。

items.en: Ripan means to cut down grain with a sickle.
items.cn: 古英语 ripan 意为用镰刀割倒谷物。

items.en: The verb becomes repen, with short forms such as repe and rop.
items.cn: 到中古英语，动词写作 repen，并有 repe、rop 等短形式。

items.en: The figurative use of reaping rewards and consequences appears in ordinary prose.
items.cn: 十五世纪前后，reap 用于「收获回报与后果」的比喻义，进入日常散文。

items.en: The machine name combine harvester replaces the hand sickle, while the phrases about effort and consequence stay fixed.
items.cn: 联合收割机取代了手工镰刀，但关于付出与后果的固定说法一直沿用到现代英语。

note.en: Reap looks close to read and reed by spelling, and stands near harvest, gather, and mow in meaning.
note.cn: reap 在拼写上接近 read 与 reed，在意义上则与 harvest、gather、mow 相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 读；阅读，只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a tall grass that grows by water
entries.definitionCN: 芦苇，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person or machine that cuts grain
entries.definitionCN: 收割者；收割机，由 reap 加 -er 构成

entries.definition: the gathering of crops
entries.definitionCN: 收获；收成，兼指动作与结果

entries.definition: to bring things together
entries.definitionCN: 收集；聚拢，侧重「收拢」而非「割」

entries.definition: to cut grass or grain with a blade
entries.definitionCN: 割（草或谷物），侧重割、不强调收获

normalIntro.en: Reap is the sickle word: cutting a crop and gathering it, then any reward that follows long work.
normalIntro.cn: reap 是「镰刀」的词：割下庄稼再收拢，后来也指长久付出之后得到的回报。

normal.en: Reap the benefits means to enjoy the good results of earlier work.
normal.cn: reap the benefits 指享受先前努力带来的好处。

normal.en: Reap what one has sown links the harvest to its seed in advance.
normal.cn: reap what one has sown 把收割与当初撒下的种子连在一起。

normal.en: A reaper is one who cuts, and in capital letters Reaper names death.
normal.cn: reaper 指收割的人，大写 Reaper 则指死神。

normal.en: Compare mow: mow cuts grass for tidiness, reap cuts grain to keep.
normal.cn: 对比 mow：割草为整洁，收割庄稼为收藏。

normal.en: The noun harvest often takes the spot where a noun would be needed.
normal.cn: 需要名词时通常用 harvest 顶替 reap 的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a row of wheat falling as one curved blade sweeps past.
abstract.cn: 想象一排麦子在一把弯刀扫过时齐齐倒下。

abstract.en: See sheaves tied and stacked, each one leaning on the next.
abstract.cn: 看见捆好的麦束堆叠起来，一捆挨着一捆。

abstract.en: Imagine an orchard being stripped of ripe fruit in one afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个下午就把果园里熟透的果子摘光。

examples.en: The farmers will reap the barley in late July.
examples.cn: 农人将在七月下旬收割大麦。

examples.en: Small investors are beginning to reap the benefits of the new policy.
examples.cn: 小投资者正开始从新政策中获益。

examples.en: If we ignore the pollution now, our children will reap the consequences.
examples.cn: 如果我们现在无视污染，孩子们将来会承受后果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞普」——收割的农人在田埂上「瑞气普照」地笑着，因为一季好收成到手了；也可谐音「快镰」，提示的是用镰刀快速割下的动作。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ripan（用镰刀割谷物）→ 中古英语 repen → 英语 reap，核心义「割下并收拢」；一般认为更早的重构形式为 ripanan。

sensesIntro.en: Reap begins with cutting a crop, adds the gathering of the yield, then widens to rewards for effort, to bitter consequences, and to the old image of death.
sensesIntro.cn: reap 从「割庄稼」开始，加上「收拢产物」，再扩展到努力得到的回报、苦涩的后果，以及旧有的死亡意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved blade sweeping through standing grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：弯刀扫过直立的麦秆。

branches.en: Cutting the crop is the oldest literal sense.
branches.cn: 割庄稼是最古老的字面义。

branches.en: Gathering the yield completes the cutting.
branches.cn: 收拢产物是「割」的完成。

branches.en: Good results of effort are the sweet harvest.
branches.cn: 努力得到的回报是甘甜的收成。

branches.en: Bad results of behaviour are the bitter harvest.
branches.cn: 行为带来的坏结果则是苦涩的收成。

branches.en: Rewards and consequences both follow from what was sown earlier.
branches.cn: 回报与后果都源自当初种下的东西。

intro.en: Reap is a short native verb with a small family: reaper, reaping, and the compound reaping machine.
intro.cn: reap 是简短的本土动词，词族不大：reaper、reaping 以及收割机的说法。

latinIntro.en: Reap has no Latin ancestor, but its near neighbour harvest reaches through the Old English haerfest, so the family note is brief.
latinIntro.cn: reap 没有拉丁语祖先，近邻 harvest 则经由古英语 haerfest 而来，所以这里的同源说明从简。

items.example: Old English ripan is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 ripan 是直接祖先。

items.meaning: to cut and gather a crop
items.example: Reap keeps the sickle sense to the present.
items.exampleCN: reap 把镰刀的含义一直保留到今天。

items.example: The suffix -er forms reaper.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 reaper。

items.example: Reaper names the person and then the machine.
items.exampleCN: reaper 先指人，后指机器。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms reaping.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 reaping。

items.meaning: the act of cutting a crop
items.example: Reaping is the act named as a noun.
items.exampleCN: reaping 是把动作名词化。

items.example: Harvest is the noun partner of reap.
items.exampleCN: harvest 是 reap 的名词搭档。

items.example: A sickle is the tool that reap describes.
items.exampleCN: 镰刀正是 reap 描述的那件工具。

items.example: Sow is the opposite action, set before reap.
items.exampleCN: sow 是相反的动作，发生在 reap 之前。

definition_zh: 收割者；收割机；死神
definition_en: a person or machine that cuts and gathers a crop; also a grim figure who cuts down lives
core_image: 弯月形的镰刀贴地一挥，麦穗齐根倒下
scene: 秋日傍晚，农人弯腰挥镰，一束束麦穗在他脚边倒下。The reaper worked along the edge of the field until the last light faded.
sceneCN: 这里 reaper 是「收割者」（第 2 个义项：在田间收割庄稼的人）；句意：收割者沿着田边一路劳作，直到最后一缕光消失。

pos.zh: 收割者；收割机；（大写）死神

derivatives.zh: 收割；收获（加后缀 -er 构成执行动作的名词）
收割；收获（动词加 -ing 作名词）
可收割的（reap 加后缀 -able 构成）

senses.title: A figure who cuts lives short
senses.definition: a poetic figure shown with a scythe, who stands for death
senses.definitionCN: 以镰刀为形象、象征死亡的拟人形象
senses.example: In the old painting, the reaper stands beside the open grave.
senses.exampleCN: 在那幅老画里，死神站在敞开的墓穴旁。
senses.why: The verb reap means to cut down a crop, so a figure who cuts people down reads naturally as death itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词 reap 本义是「割倒庄稼」，于是把人「割倒」的形象就自然读作死亡本身。

senses.title: Someone who harvests a crop
senses.definition: a person who cuts and gathers grain or other crops by hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手割下并收拢谷物等庄稼的人
senses.example: The reaper bent low over the wheat with a small sickle.
senses.exampleCN: 收割者拿着小镰刀弯下腰去割麦子。
senses.why: The English agent suffix -er turns the action of reaping into the person who performs it.
senses.whyCN: 英语后缀 -er 把「收割」这一动作变成做这件事的人，于是 reap 加 -er 就是收割者。

senses.title: A machine that cuts grain
senses.definition: a machine with a cutting bar and revolving blades that cuts standing grain
senses.definitionCN: 带有切割刀杆和旋转刀片的机器，用来割倒尚未收割的谷物
senses.example: The reaper swept across the barley field in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 收割机只用了一个下午就扫过了整片大麦田。
senses.why: When machines replaced hands, the old name for the worker was simply carried over to the tool.
senses.whyCN: 机器取代人手之后，原本称呼人的旧词就直接挪给了工具，所以收割机也叫 reaper。

senses.title: One who gathers in a reward
senses.definition: someone who enjoys the results or rewards of an effort
senses.definitionCN: 享受到某份努力成果或报酬的人
senses.example: The reaper of that quiet patience was a healthier body.
senses.exampleCN: 那份安静的耐心带来的收获，是一个更健康的身体。
senses.why: The metaphor of harvest carries over to abstract gains, so a reaper can be anyone who gathers results.
senses.whyCN: 收割的比喻延伸到抽象的收益上，于是收获者也可以指任何得到成果的人。

intro.en: Reaper joins Old English ripan, to reap, with the English suffix -er, and first names someone who cuts down grain.
intro.cn: reaper 由古英语 ripan（收割）加英语后缀 -er 构成，最初指割谷物的人。

items.en: The reconstructed verb resembles a cutting word and is related to the root seen in modern reap.
items.cn: 重构出来的动词与「切割」义相关，其词根见诸现代英语 reap（一般认为如此）。

items.en: Ripan means to cut grain or a field of crops.
items.cn: 古英语 ripan 意为割谷物、割田里的庄稼。

items.en: A worker noun built from the verb appears in texts about harvest labour.
items.cn: 由这个动词构成的人物名词出现在描写收割劳作的文献里。

items.en: Reper and reaper name the person who carries the harvest to the barn.
items.cn: 中古英语 reper、reaper 指出手收割、把粮食运进谷仓的人。

items.en: The name moves by metonymy from the worker to the cutting machine.
items.cn: 这个词通过「以人代物」的转喻，从劳动者转指切割的机器。

items.en: The capitalised Grim Reaper fixes the figure of death in fiction and film.
items.cn: 大写形式的 Grim Reaper 在小说与电影中固定为死亡的形象。

note.en: Reaper is the doer noun of reap, and it stands beside harvest words and, by metaphor, death.
note.cn: reaper 是 reap 的执行者名词，与收割类的词相邻，并通过比喻与死亡相接。

normalIntro.en: Reaper is reap plus the doer ending -er: the one who cuts and gathers.
normalIntro.cn: reaper 就是 reap 加表示「做事的人」的后缀 -er：动手收割的那一位。

normal.en: To reap is to cut grain, so a reaper is anyone who does that cutting.
normal.cn: reap 是割谷物的意思，所以 reaper 就是动手收割的那一位。

normal.en: As you sow, so you reap: the reaper gathers what was planted earlier.
normal.cn: 「种瓜得瓜」，收割者收的是早先种下的东西。

normal.en: The machinery sense came later: the reaper cuts the standing crop.
normal.cn: 「收割机」这个义项出现得更晚：reaper 割倒的还是站着的庄稼。

normal.en: Capitalised, the Grim Reaper turns the cutter of grain into the cutter of lives.
normal.cn: 首字母大写的 Grim Reaper 把割庄稼的人变成了收割生命的人。

normal.en: Compare harvester: harvester underlines the storage of the crop, reaper the cutting.
normal.cn: 对比 harvester：harvester 强调把粮食收起来，reaper 强调把它割下来。

abstract.en: See a thin hooded figure on the edge of the field, a scythe resting on the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象田边站着一位披斗篷的瘦高身影，镰刀搭在地上。

abstract.en: Picture a row of wheat falling as one even sweep of the blade passes by.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃平平一挥，一整排麦子整齐地倒下。

abstract.en: Hear the steady click of the mower blades moving across the field.
abstract.cn: 想象听见收割机刀片扫过整片田地时那规律的咔嗒声。

examples.en: The reaper moved down the wheat row, cutting in slow, even sweeps.
examples.cn: 收割者沿着麦垄一路向前，一刀一刀平稳地割着。

examples.en: In many old stories, a reaper with a scythe waits at the moment of death.
examples.cn: 在许多古老的故事里，手持镰刀的死神会在死亡的时刻等候。

examples.en: A single reaper could once cut as much grain as several helpers could bind.
examples.cn: 从前一个收割者割下的谷物，能抵好几名帮手捆扎的量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞普」——读起来像 reap 的谐音，手起刀落，「瑞普」就是那个割麦子的。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 → ripan（割、收割，一般认为与原始日耳曼语若干「切割」义动词同源）→ 加英语后缀 -er（做事的人），构成 reaper，核心义「割」。

sensesIntro.en: Reaper starts from the literal cutter of grain, then moves to the machine, to the person who gathers results, and to the death figure.
sensesIntro.cn: reaper 先指字面上割谷物的人，再转指收割机，进而指收获成果的人，最后指象征死亡的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sickle sweeping low and the wheat falling at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：镰刀贴地一挥，麦穗在刀刃边倒下。

branches.en: The hand harvest gives the concrete everyday sense.
branches.cn: 手工收割是具体、日常的义项。

branches.en: Machines inherit the worker name.
branches.cn: 机器的义项继承了劳动者的旧名。

branches.en: Abstract gains are the harvest metaphor extended.
branches.cn: 抽象的收益是收割比喻的延伸。

branches.en: Cutting down people gives the death figure.
branches.cn: 把人割倒的联想长出了死亡形象的义项。

branches.en: Person, machine, and death all share the one scythe image.
branches.cn: 人、机器与死神三者共享同一把镰刀的意象。

intro.en: Reaper is a small English word family: reap, reaper, reaping, and the -er doer suffix.
intro.cn: reaper 属于一个小型的英语词族：reap、reaper、reaping，以及表示执行者的后缀 -er。

latinIntro.cn: reap 是本土日耳曼语动词，没有拉丁语源头，所以这里的拉丁条目只列出与收割义场最接近的拉丁相关词。

definition_zh: 叛逆的；反抗的；桀骜不驯的
definition_en: refusing to obey rules, parents, or an authority, and often acting against them

scene: 饭桌上一提门禁时间，少年就把勺子一放，径直回房锁门。Every rule at home felt like a challenge to the rebellious boy.

pos.zh: 叛逆的；反抗的；桀骜不驯的

derivatives.zh: 反叛；反抗（rebellious 所由派生的基础词）
叛乱；造反（拉丁语来源的名词）
叛逆；桀骜（rebellious 加名词后缀 -ness）
叛逆地；违抗地（加副词后缀 -ly）

senses.title: Defying rules or control
senses.definition: refusing to obey rules, parents, or teachers, and often pushing back against them
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝遵守规矩、父母的管教或老师的要求，往往还对着干
senses.example: His rebellious attitude made every curfew a long argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他那种叛逆的态度让每次宵禁都变成一场漫长的争吵。
senses.why: The Latin base rebellis means one who starts war against a power again, so a rebellious person reopens the fight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 rebellis 意为「再次向当权者开战的人」，所以叛逆的人就是把对抗重新挑起来的人。

senses.title: Refusing an established authority
senses.titleCN: 反抗当权者的；聚众对抗的
senses.definition: rising up against a government, a ruler, or another established authority
senses.definitionCN: 起来对抗政府、统治者或其它既有权威的
senses.example: The rebellious provinces closed their ports to the royal fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 反叛的各省对王室舰队关闭了港口。
senses.why: The word grew out of warfare: rebel and rebellion name armed resistance, and the adjective keeps that political force.
senses.whyCN: 这个词长在战争的语境里：rebel、rebellion 都指武装反抗，形容词也保留了这种政治上的力量。

senses.title: Resisting conventional taste
senses.definition: deliberately breaking with accepted styles, customs, or artistic conventions
senses.definitionCN: 刻意背离公认的风格、习俗或艺术传统的
senses.example: They wore rebellious colours because everyone else wore grey.
senses.exampleCN: 他们穿着反传统的颜色，因为其他人都穿灰色。
senses.why: Once the political struggle fades, the same impulse to break with what is required turns into fashion and art.
senses.whyCN: 政治对抗的色彩淡去之后，同样的「偏要违抗」的冲动就转移到了时尚与艺术上。

senses.title: Hard to control or cure
senses.titleCN: 难以控制的；难以治愈的
senses.definition: stubbornly refusing to respond to efforts to control, cure, or manage it
senses.definitionCN: 顽固地不回应控制、治疗或管理的努力
senses.example: The rebellious fever went back up each time the medicine was reduced.
senses.exampleCN: 每次一减药，那种难缠的高烧就又烧回来了。
senses.why: Anything that will not bow to a force can be called rebellious, even a disease or a machine.
senses.whyCN: 任何不肯向力量低头的东西都可以叫 rebellious，连疾病和机器也不例外。

intro.en: Rebellious comes from the Latin adjective rebellis, meaning that wages war again, built with the prefix re- and the war word bellum.
intro.cn: rebellious 来自拉丁语 re-（再次）加 bellum（战争）构成的 Rebellis（再次开战），核心仍是「再次举起武器」。

items.en: Bellum means war, and re- means again or back.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellum 意为战争，前缀 re- 表示再次、反过来。

items.en: Rebellare means to renew war against a power after a surrender.
items.cn: rebellare 意为投降之后再度对某势力发动战争。

items.en: Rebellir and rebelle carry the sense of renewal of war into French.
items.cn: 古法语 rebellir、rebelle 把「重开战端」的意义带进法语。

items.en: Rebel names one who refuses lawful obedience to a ruler.
items.cn: 中古英语 rebel 指拒绝合法服从统治者的人。

items.en: Rebellious, with the Latin adjectival ending -ous, describes such a person.
items.cn: 带拉丁形容词词尾 -ous 的 rebellious 用来形容这样的人，见于十四世纪。

items.en: The adjective widens to fashion, manners, and anything that resists control.
items.cn: 现代英语把这一形容词扩展到时尚、举止乃至任何抗拒控制的事物。

note.en: Rebellious is the adjective of rebel, built on the same Latin war root as rebellion, well known in revolt and mutiny.
note.cn: rebellious 是 rebel 的形容词，与 rebellion 共用拉丁语「战争」词根，义场上与 revolt、mutiny 相邻。

entries.definition: a person who rises against authority, or to rise against it
an organised attempt to change or leave a government by force
to refuse an offer sharply
entries.definitionCN: 断然拒绝，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: openly refusing to obey
refusing to obey a person in charge
willing to obey

normalIntro.en: Rebellious is built on re- plus bellum, war: the one who goes back to war against whoever rules.
normalIntro.cn: rebellious 由 re-（再次）加 bellum（战争）构成：再向当权者开战的那一个。

normal.en: Rebel is the base word, so a rebellious child is a small rebel at home.
normal.cn: 基础词是 rebel，所以 rebellious 的孩子就是家里的一个小反叛者。

normal.en: Rebellion is the act, rebellious the quality, rebelliousness the noun for it.
normal.cn: rebellion 指行为本身，rebellious 指这种气质，rebelliousness 是其名词形式。

normal.en: The Latin bellum, war, hides in rebel, rebellion, and rebellious.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的 bellum（战争）藏在 rebel、rebellion、rebellious 三个词里。

normal.en: Common partners are teenager, spirit, behaviour, and streak.
normal.cn: 常见搭配搭档是 teenager、spirit、behaviour 与 streak。

normal.en: Compare defiant: defiant refuses face to face, rebellious can also be a lasting trait.
normal.cn: 对比 defiant：defiant 强调当面顶撞，rebellious 也可以是长期的性格。

abstract.en: Picture a teenager dropping a fork on the table and walking out of the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个少年把餐叉往桌上一放，起身走出房间。

abstract.en: See a crowd pushing a heavy gate shut against armed soldiers on the other side.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人把厚重的大门推上，把门外的武装士兵挡在外面。

abstract.en: Think of a jacket in bright orange worn on a day when everyone else wears grey.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都穿灰色的时候，有人偏穿一件亮橙色外套。

examples.en: She was rebellious at sixteen and calm by twenty five.
examples.cn: 她十六岁时很叛逆，到了二十五岁就沉稳了。

examples.en: The government moved troops into the rebellious northern towns.
examples.cn: 政府把军队开进了反叛的北部城镇。

examples.en: His music was too rebellious for the radio stations of that decade.
examples.cn: 他的音乐对那个年代的电台来说太反传统了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞贝利厄斯」——听上去像「锐比利」的夸张说法，锐利得不服气，就是一副桀骜的样子。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ bellum（战争）→ rebellare（重新开战）→ rebellis（再次开战的人）→ 古法语 rebelle → 英语 rebel；加英语形容词词尾 -ous 后得 rebellious。

sensesIntro.en: Rebellious begins with personal defiance, widens to political revolt, then to breaking with convention, and finally to anything that resists control.
sensesIntro.cn: rebellious 从个人层面的不服管教开始，扩展到政治上的反抗，再延伸到背离常规，最后泛指一切抗拒控制的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young hand pushing away the hand that holds it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手推开那只伸过来牵它的手。

branches.en: Defiance at home and school is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 家庭与学校里不服管教是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Political revolt is where the war root surfaces plainly.
branches.cn: 政治反抗是「战争」词根最直白的出口。

branches.en: Breaking with style turns the fight into taste.
branches.cn: 背离风格把对抗变成了审美趣味。

branches.en: Anything that resists control borrows the same adjective.
branches.cn: 任何抗拒控制的事物都借用了同一个形容词。

branches.en: A stubborn teenager and an angry province share the same refusal.
branches.cn: 执拗的少年和愤怒的省份共享同一种「不听话」。

intro.en: Rebellious sits in a Latin word family: the prefix re-, the war word bellum, the verb rebel, and the noun rebellion.
intro.cn: rebellious 属于一组拉丁语来源的词族：前缀 re-、表示战争的 bellum，以及动词 rebel 和名词 rebellion。

latinIntro.en: Latin bellum, war, and re-, again, make rebellare, to wage war again, and the adjective rebellis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bellum（战争）与前缀 re-（再次）合称 rebellare（再度开战），由此得出形容词 rebellis。

items.example: The prefix re- in rebellare means war a second time.
items.exampleCN: rebellare 中的前缀 re- 指第二次开战。

items.example: Bellum is the war behind rebellious.
items.exampleCN: bellum 是 rebellious 背后的「战争」。

items.example: To rebellare was to take up arms a second time.
items.exampleCN: rebellare 就是第二次拿起武器。

items.example: Rebellis labelled the province that broke the truce.
items.exampleCN: rebellis 用来称呼破坏停战的那个行省。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous turns rebellion into rebellious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把 rebellion 变成 rebellious。

items.meaning: to rise against authority; a person who does
items.example: The workers rebelled against the new schedule.
items.exampleCN: 工人们反抗新的排班表。

items.meaning: an armed or open refusal to obey
items.example: The rebellion lasted a full year.
items.exampleCN: 那场叛乱持续了整整一年。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms rebelliousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 rebelliousness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms rebelliously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 rebelliously。

latinEntries.meaning: to wage war, from bellum and gerere

definition_zh: 重播；转播
definition_en: to send out a programme again that has already been broadcast, or to pass on another station programme
core_image: 同一条电波被天线接住，经过放大器再度发往更远的地方
scene: 深夜的收音机里，主持人在节目末尾宣布：下周同一时间将重播这期访谈。The station will rebroadcast the interview next Sunday evening.
sceneCN: 这里 rebroadcast 是「重播」（第 1 个义项：把已经播出过的节目再播一次）；句意：这家电台将于下周日晚上重播这次访谈。

pos.zh: 重播；转播
重播的节目；转播

collocations.phrase: a rebroadcast of an old show

derivatives.zh: 播送；广播（rebroadcast 的基础词）
播音员；广播机构（broadcast 加 -er）
重播；转播活动（rebroadcast 加 -ing）

senses.title: To air a programme again
senses.definition: to broadcast a programme again after it has already been shown or heard
senses.definitionCN: 节目已经播出过之后，再播送一次
senses.example: The channel will rebroadcast the final in full next weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个频道下个周末会把决赛完整地重播一遍。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again, so the whole idea is broadcast repeated once more.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再一次」，整词的意思就是把 broadcast 再播一遍，再播正是重播。

senses.title: To pass on another station signal
senses.definition: to receive a programme from one station or network and send it out again to more people
senses.definitionCN: 接收某个电台或电视台的节目，再向外发送给更多人
senses.example: Local stations rebroadcast the national news at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 地方电台在七点转播全国新闻。
senses.why: When the source is another station, the repeated broadcast becomes a relay, and English uses the same word for it.
senses.whyCN: 当来源是另一家电台时，再次播送就变成了接力的转播，英语仍然用同一个词表示。

senses.title: A repeated broadcast
senses.definition: a broadcast that is shown or heard again, or the slot or showing in which it appears
senses.definitionCN: 被再次播出的一档节目，或播出它的时间段、放映场次
senses.example: The late rebroadcast drew more listeners than the live one.
senses.exampleCN: 深夜的重播比直播吸引了更多听众。
senses.why: Every verb in this family can also name the thing done, so the repeated transmission becomes a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 这一家族里的动词都能指称所做的事，于是重复播送的节目就成了可数的名词。

intro.en: Rebroadcast is a modern English compound: the prefix re- plus broadcast, itself from broad and the verb cast.
intro.cn: rebroadcast 是现代英语的合成词：前缀 re-（再次）加 broadcast，而 broadcast 本身由 broad（广）与动词 cast（撒、投）构成。

items.en: Castan means to throw, and its descendant cast keeps that force.
items.cn: 古英语 castan 意为投掷，其后代 cast 保留了这一力度。

items.en: Broadcast describes the wide scattering of seed by hand.
items.cn: 十八世纪 broadcast 指用手把种子大范围撒开。

items.en: The word widens to news scattered to many people at once.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，broadcast 用于把消息同时散布给众多人。

items.en: Radio arrives and broadcast settles on the sending of programmes by wireless.
items.cn: 二十世纪初无线电出现，broadcast 固定指用无线电播送节目。

items.en: The prefix re- is added for sending the same programme out again.
items.cn: 加上前缀 re-，表示把同一档节目再播送一次。

items.en: Rebroadcast covers repeats, relays, and the repeated programmes themselves.
items.cn: 现代英语的 rebroadcast 涵盖重播、转播以及被重播的节目本身。

note.en: Rebroadcast is built on broadcast, and it stands beside send and transmit verbs while the -cast element goes back to a throwing verb.
note.cn: rebroadcast 建立在 broadcast 之上，旁边是同源的 cast 以及 send、transmit 一类播送词。

entries.definition: to send out a programme by radio or television
to say what is likely to happen, from cast forward
entries.definitionCN: 预报（把判断向前抛出），与 cast 同源

entries.definition: to throw, or to give out or assign
to show or do something again
to send out signals or programmes
to pass a signal on from one point to another

normalIntro.en: Rebroadcast is broadcast with re- in front: the same programme sent out a second time.
normalIntro.cn: rebroadcast 就是在 broadcast 前面加 re-：同一档节目被发送了第二次。

normal.en: Broad means wide, so to broadcast is to scatter a message out widely.
normal.cn: broad 是「广」，broadcast 就是把消息广泛地撒出去。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again, so rebroadcast is broadcast one more time.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，所以 rebroadcast 就是把广播再播一次。

normal.en: Cast is the throwing verb inside both broadcast and forecast.
normal.cn: cast 是「抛」这个动词，它同样藏在 broadcast 和 forecast 里面。

normal.en: The past form usually stays rebroadcast, like broadcast itself.
normal.cn: 过去式通常仍写作 rebroadcast，和 broadcast 一样不变。

normal.en: Compare relay: relay moves a signal onward from another point, rebroadcast repeats a whole programme.
normal.cn: 对比 relay：relay 强调把信号从中继点转出去，rebroadcast 强调整档节目再播一遍。

abstract.en: See a radio tower lighting up again with the same voice it sent out a week ago.
abstract.cn: 想象一座发射塔再次亮起，传出一周前那同一种声音。

abstract.en: Follow the signal being caught by a small antenna and pushed out even further.
abstract.cn: 想象信号被小天线接住，又被推向更远的地方。

abstract.en: Hear the tape of a finished show starting to play over again at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜时分，一盘早已播完的节目录音又从头放起。

examples.en: The network will rebroadcast the opening ceremony on Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 这家电视网将在周日早上重播开幕式。

examples.en: Village stations often rebroadcast programmes from the capital.
examples.cn: 村里的电台常常转播首都的节目。

examples.en: A late rebroadcast of the debate reached an audience twice the size of the live one.
examples.cn: 那场辩论的深夜重播，听众规模是直播时的两倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞布若德卡斯特」——re 开头就是「再来一次」，broadcast 是「广撒」，连起来就是再广撒一遍。这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: re-（再次）+ broadcast（由 broad 广 + 古英语 castan 投掷得名）→ rebroadcast，核心义「同一节目的再次播送」。

sensesIntro.en: Rebroadcast first means airing the same programme again, then passing on a signal from another station, and finally the repeated broadcast itself.
sensesIntro.cn: rebroadcast 先指把同一档节目再播一遍，再指转发其他电台的信号，最后指被重播的节目本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave caught by one antenna and sent out again further.
core.cn: 核心意象：电波被一根天线接住，又被发往更远处。

branches.en: Airing the same programme again is the plain re- sense.
branches.cn: 把同一档节目再播一遍，是前缀 re- 最直白的义项。

branches.en: Relaying from another station adds a second sender.
branches.cn: 从别的电台转发，等于多了第二个发送方。

branches.en: The repeated broadcast becomes a noun you can count.
branches.cn: 重播的节目本身变成了可数的名词。

branches.en: Repeat and relay both grow from one broadcast sent twice.
branches.cn: 重播和转播都从「同一个广播发了两次」长出来。

branches.en: A relayed signal and a repeated show are heard by new audiences.
branches.cn: 转播的信号与重播的节目都让新的听众听见。

intro.en: Rebroadcast combines the prefix re- with the compound broadcast, and its family includes broadcaster and rebroadcasting.
intro.cn: rebroadcast 由前缀 re- 与合成词 broadcast 组合而成，其词族还包括 broadcaster 与 rebroadcasting。

latinIntro.en: Neither broadcast nor cast has a Latin parent; the Latin relatives here belong to the world of spreading and carrying words.
latinIntro.cn: broadcast 与 cast 都没有拉丁语源头；这里列出的拉丁条目只属于「散播、传递」这一意义世界的相关词。

items.example: The prefix re- makes rebroadcast of broadcast.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把 broadcast 变成 rebroadcast。

items.example: A broad signal reaches many homes.
items.exampleCN: 宽泛的信号能到达许多家庭。

items.example: Seeds were once cast by hand across a field.
items.exampleCN: 人们曾用手把种子撒遍整片田地。

items.example: The concert was broadcast across the country.
items.exampleCN: 这场音乐会在全国播出。

items.meaning: a station or person that broadcasts
items.example: The broadcaster holds the rights to the match.
items.exampleCN: 这家广播机构拥有这场比赛的权利。

items.example: Rebroadcasting needs a second licence.
items.exampleCN: 重播需要另一份许可。

items.meaning: to say in advance what will happen
items.example: Forecast and broadcast share the throwing verb cast.
items.exampleCN: forecast 与 broadcast 共用「投」这个动词。

items.example: The hill station relays the signal inland.
items.exampleCN: 山上的电台把信号转发到内陆。

items.meaning: to send out or do again
items.example: The channel repeats the talk show on Sunday.
items.exampleCN: 这个频道周日照例重播那档脱口秀。

definition_zh: 反驳；驳斥；举反证；顶回去
definition_en: to argue that a statement, claim, or charge is false, usually by offering evidence or reasons against it
core_image: 把对方抛过来的话原样顶回他脸上
scene: 辩论赛上，对方提出新证据，主队辩手立刻站起来逐条驳回。On stage, the opposing team gave new evidence, and the debater stood up at once to rebut each point.
sceneCN: 这里 rebut 是「反驳、驳斥」（第 1 个义项：用理由或证据推翻对方的说法）；句意：辩论赛上，对方提出新证据，主队辩手立刻站起来逐条驳回。

pos.zh: 反驳；驳斥；举反证
进行反驳；回击
（法律）反驳；反证（旧用法）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 rebut 加名词后缀 -al 构成，义为「反驳；驳斥；反证」
由 rebut 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，法律用语，义为「可反驳的；可推翻的」
由 rebut 加表示「人或动作」的后缀 -er 构成，旧法律用语，指「反驳；答辩人」

senses.title: To argue back against a claim
senses.definition: to argue that a statement or claim is false by giving reasons or evidence against it
senses.definitionCN: 通过给出理由或证据，论证某个说法或主张不成立
senses.example: The minister tried to rebut the report with new figures.
senses.exampleCN: 部长试图用新数据反驳那份报告。
senses.why: The Old French prefix re- means back, and bouter means to push, so rebut is to push an argument back at the person who made it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语前缀 re- 表示「往回」，bouter 表示「推」，所以 rebut 就是把对方的话推回给他，这就是正面反驳。

senses.title: To answer a charge in law
senses.definition: to answer a legal charge or accusation by showing evidence that it is not true
senses.definitionCN: 用证据回应法律指控，证明指控不成立
senses.example: The defence rebutted the allegation with phone records.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方用电话记录反驳了该项指控。
senses.why: Legal usage keeps the fighting image: the accused pushes the charge back with proof of innocence.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法保留了「对抗」的画面：被告用无罪的证据把指控顶回去，于是这个动作被制度化成了「举反证」。

senses.title: To push something back physically
senses.definition: to push or force something back, a physical sense now found mostly in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物推回或弹回，这一物理义项如今多见于旧文献
senses.example: The wave rebuted the small boat from the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 浪把小船从礁石边顶了回去。
senses.why: This is the original bodily action of bouter, to push, before the word turned into a verbal joust.
senses.whyCN: 这是 bouter（推）最初的身体动作，在这个词变成口头交锋之前，「顶回去」正是字面本义。

senses.title: To refute by reason and evidence
senses.definition: to prove that an idea or presumption is not valid
senses.definitionCN: 证明某个观点或推定并不成立
senses.example: The study rebuts the idea that memory declines only with age.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究推翻「记忆只会随年龄衰退」的观点。
senses.why: Once pushing back is done with data, rebut shifts from countering words to knocking down a proposition.
senses.whyCN: 当回顶的工具变成数据时，rebut 就从「顶回话语」升级为「打倒一个命题」，强调结果是被证明不成立。

senses.title: To reply sharply in a debate
senses.definition: to respond quickly and sharply in an argument or discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在争论或讨论中迅速而尖锐地回应
senses.example: She rebutted his interruption before he could finish.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话还没说完，就被她当场驳回。
senses.why: The push-back image gives the word its speed: a rebuttal throws the attack back before it lands.
senses.whyCN: 「推回去」的画面自带速度感：反驳是在攻击落地之前就把它扔回去，所以 rebut 常带「及时、干脆」的味道。

senses.title: To overturn a presumption by evidence
senses.definition: to offer evidence strong enough to overturn a legal presumption
senses.definitionCN: 提供足以推翻某项法律推定的证据
senses.example: The documents rebut the presumption of consent.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件推翻了关于同意的推定。
senses.why: A presumption stands until someone pushes it down; rebut names exactly that pushing down with proof.
senses.whyCN: 推定在被人推翻之前一直成立；rebut 正好指「用证据把它压下去」这个动作，所以法律英语里形成固定说法。

intro.en: Rebut comes from Old French rebouter, to push back, formed from re- back and bouter to push, a word of uncertain Germanic origin.
intro.cn: rebut 来自古法语 rebouter（推回），由 re-（往回）与 bouter（推）构成，bouter 的词源一般认为源自日耳曼语，具体形式存疑。

items.en: The verb bouter, to push or thrust, is generally traced to a Germanic source, though the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 bouter（推、撞）一般认为源自日耳曼语，具体词形来源不确定。

items.en: Rebouter means to push back or drive back, often in riding and fighting.
items.cn: rebouter 意为推回、击退，常见于骑马与搏斗语境。

items.en: In legal French the verb names a reply that drives back a charge.
items.cn: 在法律法语中，这个动词指把指控顶回去的答辩。

items.en: Rebouten enters English, first in law and then in general argument.
items.cn: rebouten 进入英语，先用于法律，后用于一般争论。

items.en: Rebuttal and rebuttable grow from the verb, and rebut is standard in debate and legal writing.
items.cn: rebuttal 与 rebuttable 由该动词派生，rebut 成为辩论与法律写作的标准用词。

note.en: Rebut belongs to the rebuttal family of legal and debate vocabulary, and it sits next to refute, contradict, and disprove.
note.cn: rebut 属于 bat 词根的法律与辩论词汇家族，与 refute、contradict、disprove 意义相邻。

entries.definition: a reply that argues against a claim or charge
entries.definitionCN: 由 rebut 加 -al 构成，义为「反驳；驳斥」

entries.definition: able to be argued against or overturned
entries.definitionCN: 由 rebut 加 -able 构成，义为「可反驳的」

entries.definition: to reject an offer or advance abruptly
entries.definitionCN: 同样是 re- 加推撞类词根，但 rebuff 指「断然拒绝」，与 rebut 只是拼写相近、用法不同

entries.definition: to prove a statement or person to be wrong
entries.definitionCN: 驳倒；证明是错的；比 rebut 更强调「证伪成功」

entries.definition: to say the opposite of what someone has said
entries.definitionCN: 反驳；与……相矛盾；只表示说了相反的话，不一定带证据

entries.definition: to argue that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 主张；争辩；方向相反，是提出主张而不是驳倒主张

normalIntro.en: Rebut is a push-back word: re- means back, so you push a claim back into the face of the one who made it.
normalIntro.cn: rebut 是一个「推回去」的词：re- 表示往回，把对方的说法推回他面前。

normal.en: Rebuttal is the noun of rebut, and it names the reply itself.
normal.cn: rebuttal 是 rebut 的名词形式，指那番反驳本身。

normal.en: Rebuttable evidence can still be pushed back.
normal.cn: rebuttable evidence 是可以被推翻的证据。

normal.en: You rebut a claim, an argument, or a charge, not a person.
normal.cn: rebut 的宾语是说法、论点或指控，而不是人。

normal.en: In law, to rebut the presumption is to overturn it with proof.
normal.cn: 法律里 rebut the presumption 就是用证据推翻推定。

normal.en: Compare refute: rebut answers a claim, refute proves it false, and refute is the stronger word.
normal.cn: 对比 refute：rebut 是回击说法，refute 是证明其错，refute 语气更强。

abstract.en: Picture a ball thrown at you and thrown straight back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个球朝你扔来，你又原样扔回去。

abstract.en: Imagine a lawyer standing up to hand back a charge with proof.
abstract.cn: 想象律师站起来，拿着证据把指控送回去。

abstract.en: Think of a gate that pushes back anything it does not take in.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门把所有进不来的东西都顶回去。

examples.en: The company rebutted the claim that its products were unsafe.
examples.cn: 该公司反驳了其产品不安全的说法。

examples.en: Her lawyer quickly rebutted the charge of fraud.
examples.cn: 她的律师迅速驳斥了欺诈指控。

examples.en: The defence counsel asked for time to rebut the new evidence.
examples.cn: 辩护律师请求给予时间反驳新证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞巴特」——瑞巴特站起来，把对手的话一句句「顶」回去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 re-（往回）+ bouter（推、撞）→ rebouter（推回；击退）→ 英语 rebut（反驳；顶回），核心义「把话推回去」。

sensesIntro.en: Rebut starts from pushing a claim back in debate, then extends to legal rebuttal with proof, and finally to overturning a presumption.
sensesIntro.cn: rebut 从辩论中把说法推回去开始，延伸到法律上用证据反证，最后发展为推翻推定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thrown claim pushed straight back.
core.cn: 核心意象：把抛过来的说法原样顶回去。

branches.en: Debate rebuttal is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 辩论中的反驳是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Answering a charge is the legal courtroom sense.
branches.cn: 回应指控是法庭上的法律义项。

branches.en: Pushing back physically is the old literal sense.
branches.cn: 把东西推回去是古老的字面义项。

branches.en: A sharp reply and a reasoned proof are both ways of defeating an argument.
branches.cn: 尖锐回击与有理有据的证明都是打掉对方论点的途径。

branches.en: Legal rebuttal works by overturning a stated presumption.
branches.cn: 法律上的反驳，具体做法就是推翻被写明的那项推定。

intro.en: Rebut is built from the Old French prefix re-, the verb stem bout-, and the English inflection, with rebuttal and rebuttable as its family.
intro.cn: rebut 由古法语前缀 re-、动词词干 bout- 和英语变形构成，词族成员有 rebuttal 与 rebuttable。

latinIntro.en: Rebut has no Latin father word: it comes through Old French, and the re- prefix alone is shared with Latin.
latinIntro.cn: rebut 没有直接的拉丁语父词，它经由古法语传入英语，只有前缀 re- 与拉丁语同源。

items.example: The prefix re- gives rebut its sense of pushing back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 赋予 rebut「推回去」的含义。

items.example: The stem bout- comes from bouter, to push.
items.exampleCN: 词干 bout- 来自 bouter（推）。

items.meaning: to push back, to drive back
items.example: Rebouter is the immediate source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: rebouter 是英语词的直接来源。

items.meaning: verb ending of the borrowed stem
items.example: The final -t stays from the French form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -t 保留了法语形式的痕迹。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms rebutted.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 rebutted。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms rebutting with a doubled t.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 rebutting，注意辅音 t 要双写。

items.example: The suffix -al forms rebuttal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 rebuttal。

items.example: The suffix -able forms rebuttable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 rebuttable。

items.example: The suffix -er forms the old legal word rebutter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成旧法律词 rebutter。

latinEntries.example: Latin re- matches the French prefix in rebut.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 re- 与 rebut 中的法语前缀一致。

definition_zh: 桀骜不驯的；倔强不服从的；难对付的；抗拒处理的
definition_en: refusing to obey authority, follow orders, or change behaviour, and resisting control with stubborn energy
core_image: 一头驴被人拉缰绳，却后腿蹬地、尥着蹄子往回踢
scene: 整支队伍都按规定排队，只有那个新兵总也纠正不过来。The whole squad lined up as ordered, yet that new recruit remained stubbornly recalcitrant.
sceneCN: 这里 recalcitrant 是「倔强不听劝、怎么也纠正不过来」（第 2 个义项：抵制改变行为的努力）；句意：整支队伍都按规定排队，只有那个新兵总也纠正不过来。

pos.zh: 桀骜不驯的；倔强不服从的；难对付的
不服从者；顽固抗拒者

derivatives.zh: 由 recalcitrant 去尾加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「桀骜不驯；抗拒」
由 recalcitrant 去尾加名词后缀 -cy 构成，与 recalcitrance 同义，较罕见
由拉丁词根重构的动词，罕用，义为「尥蹶子；倔强反抗」

senses.title: Refusing to obey authority
senses.definition: stubbornly refusing to obey rules or people in authority
senses.definitionCN: 顽固地拒绝服从规则或权威
senses.example: The general had no patience for recalcitrant officers.
senses.exampleCN: 将军对拒不服从的军官毫无耐心。
senses.why: The Latin word meant kicking back with the heels, so a person who kicks against orders is literally kicking back like a mule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「用脚跟往回踢」，抗拒命令的人就像骡子尥蹶子，把权威踢回去，这是这个义项的画面基础。

senses.title: Resisting efforts to change
senses.titleCN: 固执不肯改变的；难纠正的
senses.definition: continuing to resist attempts to help, correct, or change one
senses.definitionCN: 持续抗拒帮助、纠正或改变的尝试
senses.example: The tutor was patient with a recalcitrant pupil.
senses.exampleCN: 家教对那个怎么教都不肯改的学生很有耐心。
senses.why: Kicking back does not need an enemy: any help that wants to steer you can be fought off, so the word names resistance to correction.
senses.whyCN: 「往回踢」不一定针对敌人：任何想「拉你一把」的帮助都可能被踢开，所以这个词也用来形容抗拒纠正。

senses.title: Stubbornly opposed in opinion
senses.definition: holding an opinion firmly, even stubbornly, in spite of argument
senses.definitionCN: 即使面对论辩，也执拗地坚持某种看法
senses.example: His recalcitrant view of the plan surprised even his allies.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这个计划的执拗看法连盟友都觉得意外。
senses.why: The image moves from bodies to beliefs: a stubborn opinion is one that will not be pushed back into line.
senses.whyCN: 画面从身体转向想法：执拗的观点就是推也推不回去、不肯归位的观点。

senses.title: Difficult to deal with or solve
senses.definition: used of things such as problems, diseases, or materials that resist treatment or solution
senses.definitionCN: 用于问题、疾病或材料等对处理或解决有抵抗作用的事物
senses.example: The team fought a recalcitrant software fault for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 团队与一个顽固的软件故障缠斗了数周。
senses.why: Unresponsive objects act like a kicking animal: they refuse to be made to work, so the human sense is transferred to things.
senses.whyCN: 不听话的东西就像一头发脾气的牲口，怎么弄都不肯就范；人的义项由此转到事物上。

senses.title: Resisting treatment in medicine
senses.definition: describing a disease or condition that does not respond to treatment
senses.definitionCN: 描述对治疗没有反应的疾病或病症
senses.example: Doctors struggled with a recalcitrant strain of the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们费力应对一种难以控制的感染菌株。
senses.why: A disease that kicks back against drugs repeats the animal image: it refuses to yield to the treatment pulling on it.
senses.whyCN: 对药物「踢回来」的疾病重现了牲口的画面：治疗在拉它，它就是不肯低头就范。

senses.title: A person who resists control
senses.definition: a noun for a person who continually resists control or management
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指持续抗拒管控的人
senses.example: Officials singled out the recalcitrants in the protest.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们挑出了抗议中的那些顽固分子。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun label, naming the kicking members of a group as a class.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词标签，把群体里那些「踢腿」的人归为一类来称呼。

intro.en: Recalcitrant comes from Latin recalcitrant-, the present participle of recalcitrare, to kick back, from re- back and calcitrare, to kick, from calx, heel. The word became an English adjective in the sense of disobedient.
intro.cn: recalcitrant 来自拉丁语 recalcitrant-，即 recalcitrare（往回踢）的现在分词，由 re-（往回）与 calcitrare（踢）构成，后者源于 calx（脚后跟）；进入英语后作形容词，表示「不服从」。

items.en: Calx means the heel of the foot, the body part that drives the kick.
items.cn: calx 意为脚后跟，是踢击发力的身体部位。

items.en: Calcitrare means to kick, drawn from the heel word calx.
items.cn: calcitrare 意为踢，由表示脚后跟的 calx 派生。

items.en: Recalcitrare, to kick back like a horse or mule, appears in the works of the elder Pliny.
items.cn: recalcitrare 意为像马或骡子一样往回踢，见于老普林尼的著作。

items.en: Church writers extend recalcitrare to resisting an authority, including God.
items.cn: 教会作者把 recalcitrare 扩展到抗拒权威，包括抗拒神。

items.en: Recalcitrant is recorded in English as an adjective meaning obstinately disobedient.
items.cn: 英语中的 recalcitrant 作为形容词出现，意为顽固不服从的。

items.en: The word spreads to politics, medicine, and technology for stubborn resistance to control.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到政治、医学与技术领域，表示顽固抗拒管控。

note.en: Recalcitrant is a heel-kicking word, sharing the calc- root with calcium and calcify, and it stands beside stubborn, defiant, and unruly.
note.cn: recalcitrant 是一个「用脚跟踢」的词，与 calcium、calcify 共享 calc- 词根，语义上靠近 stubborn、defiant、unruly。

entries.definition: stubborn resistance to authority or control
entries.definitionCN: 由 recalcitrant 加 -ance 构成的名词，义为「桀骜不驯；抗拒」

entries.definition: to harden by deposits of calcium
entries.definitionCN: 同 calx 词根（意为石灰、脚后跟），义为「钙化、硬化」，与 recalcitrant 只是词根相同

entries.definition: to withdraw a statement or belief publicly
entries.definitionCN: 同样是 re- 开头、含 ca 的音节，但 recant 意为「公开放弃、撤回」，与 recalcitrant 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: refusing to change your mind or behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 固执的；最常用的一般词，不特别强调对抗权威

entries.definition: openly refusing to obey
entries.definitionCN: 公然违抗的；强调当面亮出不服

entries.definition: difficult to control or discipline
entries.definitionCN: 难管束的；多形容群体或孩子，不强调个人对抗

normalIntro.en: Recalcitrant is a kicking word: re- back and calx heel, so it describes anyone who kicks back at control.
normalIntro.cn: recalcitrant 是个「踢」的词：re- 往回、calx 脚后跟，用来形容任何对管控「踢回去」的人。

normal.en: The root calc- in recalcitrant is the same heel word behind the calcium family.
normal.cn: recalcitrant 里的 calc- 与 calcium 词族同出「脚后跟、石灰」这个词。

normal.en: Recalcitrance is the noun, spelled with -ance.
normal.cn: 名词形式 recalcitrance 以 -ance 结尾。

normal.en: You can be recalcitrant to authority, or a problem can be recalcitrant to solution.
normal.cn: 人可以对权威 recalcitrant to authority，问题也可以 recalcitrant to solution。

normal.en: Compare rebellious: rebellious suggests open revolt, recalcitrant is quieter and stiffer.
normal.cn: 对比 rebellious：rebellious 指公开反叛，recalcitrant 更低调、更犟。

normal.en: The doubled t of recalcitrant follows the t of the Latin stem calcitrare.
normal.cn: recalcitrant 中的双写字母对应拉丁词干 calcitrare 里的踢击音节。

abstract.en: Picture a mule planting both heels and kicking at the rope.
abstract.cn: 想象一头骡子四蹄蹬地，对着缰绳尥蹶子。

abstract.en: Imagine a pupil crossing his arms when the teacher corrects him.
abstract.cn: 想象老师一纠正，学生就抱起双臂。

abstract.en: Think of a screw that turns the wrong way every time you push it.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗螺丝，你越拧它越往反方向退。

examples.en: The committee reported that several recalcitrant members refused to sign.
examples.cn: 委员会报告说，有几名顽固的成员拒绝签字。

examples.en: Doctors found the infection unusually recalcitrant to antibiotics.
examples.cn: 医生发现这种感染对抗生素异常顽固。

examples.en: Inflation proved recalcitrant despite repeated rate rises.
examples.cn: 尽管利率一再上调，通胀依然顽固难消。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞卡西特」——瑞卡被人拉缰绳，还死死「卡」在原地不走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 calx（脚后跟）→ calcitrare（踢）→ 拉丁语 recalcitrare（往回踢）→ recalcitrant-（往回踢的）→ 英语 recalcitrant（桀骜不驯的），核心义「尥蹶子抵抗」。

sensesIntro.en: Recalcitrant begins with an animal kicking back at its handler, then covers people who resist authority and change, and finally stubborn things and diseases.
sensesIntro.cn: recalcitrant 起于一头发怒牲口对牵它的人尥蹶子，进而指抗拒权威与改变的人，最后扩展到顽固的事物与疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mule kicking its heels back at the rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：骡子对着缰绳往后尥蹶子。

branches.en: Kicking against authority is the central sense.
branches.cn: 抗拒权威是核心义项。

branches.en: Resisting correction and holding opinions are the personal senses.
branches.cn: 抗拒纠正与执拗己见是个人层面的义项。

branches.en: Difficult problems are treated as if they had a will of their own.
branches.cn: 棘手的问题被当成有自己的意志来描写。

branches.en: A stubborn disease refuses to be corrected just like a stubborn pupil.
branches.cn: 顽固的疾病和怎么教都不改的学生一样，都拒绝被「拨正」。

branches.en: The noun names the group of people who keep kicking.
branches.cn: 名词义项把这些一直「踢腿」的人归为一类。

intro.en: Recalcitrant is built from re-, the Latin verb stem calcitr-, and the adjective ending -ant, with recalcitrance and recalcitrancy as its family.
intro.cn: recalcitrant 由前缀 re-、拉丁词干 calcitr- 和形容词词尾 -ant 构成，词族里有 recalcitrance 与 recalcitrancy。

latinIntro.en: Latin calx gives both the heel and lime, and calcitrare turns the heel into an act of kicking back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calx 既指脚后跟也指石灰，calcitrare 把脚后跟变成「往回踢」这个动作。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the idea of kicking backwards.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加上「往回踢」的方向感。

items.example: Calx also means lime, which gave the word calcium.
items.exampleCN: calx 还指石灰，这正是 calcium 一词的来源。

items.example: The stem calcitr- comes from calcitrare, to kick.
items.exampleCN: 词干 calcitr- 来自 calcitrare（踢）。

items.example: Recalcitrare is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: recalcitrare 是直接拉丁语来源。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms recalcitrant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 recalcitrant。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms recalcitrance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成 recalcitrance。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms the rare variant recalcitrancy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成较罕见的异体 recalcitrancy。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb recalcitrantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 recalcitrantly。

latinEntries.example: Calx is also the root of calcium.
latinEntries.exampleCN: calx 也是 calcium 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Recalcitrare is the direct source of recalcitrant.
latinEntries.exampleCN: recalcitrare 是 recalcitrant 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 重新捕获；夺回；再度体验；再现；追回
definition_en: to catch or take back something that was lost or had escaped, and also to bring back a past feeling or moment
core_image: 一只飞走的鸟，又被人一把抓回掌心
scene: 警察在城郊找到并带回了三天前越狱的逃犯。Police tracked and recaptured the escaped prisoner three days after he fled.
sceneCN: 这里 recapture 是「重新捕获、抓获在逃者」（第 1 个义项：抓回已经跑掉的人或物）；句意：警察在城郊找到并带回了三天前越狱的逃犯。

pos.zh: 重新捕获；夺回；再度体验；再现
重新捕获；夺回（可作不可数或单数）

derivatives.zh: 被 re- 加上前缀的基础动词，义为「捕获；夺取」
与 capture 同 capt- 词根的名词，义为「俘虏」，兼指被抓住的人
同 capt- 词根的拉丁借用词，原义「抓夺者」，现指「猛禽」

senses.title: To catch again what escaped
senses.definition: to catch again a person or animal that had escaped or been released
senses.definitionCN: 再次抓住已经逃脱或被放走的人或动物
senses.example: The zoo recaptured the ostrich before nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园在天黑前把那只鸵鸟抓了回来。
senses.why: The Latin stem capt- means seizing, and re- means again, so recapture is the same seizing act performed a second time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 capt- 表示「抓取」，前缀 re- 表示「再一次」，所以 recapture 就是把手再伸出去抓一次，把跑掉的抓住。

senses.title: To take back by force
senses.definition: to take back a place or position from an enemy or rival by force
senses.definitionCN: 从敌人或对手手中用武力夺回某地或某职位
senses.example: The army recaptured the hill after a long fight.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一场苦战，军队夺回了那座山丘。
senses.why: Land that was captured once can be captured back, so recapture names the second, reversing capture.
senses.whyCN: 一块地第一次被「capture」夺走之后，还能再抓回来，recapture 就是这个反向的、第二次的夺取。

senses.title: To win back customers or a market
senses.definition: to win back customers, attention, or market share from a competitor
senses.definitionCN: 从竞争者手中重新赢回顾客、注意力或市场份额
senses.example: The brand recaptured its share of the shoe market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌重新赢回了鞋类市场份额。
senses.why: The battlefield image moves into business: a lost share is ground to be seized again.
senses.whyCN: 战场画面搬进商场：失去的份额就像失地，需要再抓回来，于是有了商业义项。

senses.title: To experience a past feeling again
senses.definition: to feel again a feeling or mood that belonged to an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 重新感受到属于早先某个时刻的情绪或心境
senses.example: They recaptured the joy of their first winter together.
senses.exampleCN: 他们又找回了初识那年冬天的那份快乐。
senses.why: Memory works like catching: the moment was lost, and recapture seizes it again, this time inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 记忆就像抓东西：那个瞬间早已失去，recapture 把它再抓回来，只是这次是在心里抓住。

senses.title: To reproduce something exactly
senses.definition: to reproduce an original event, mood, or sound faithfully
senses.definitionCN: 忠实再现原来的事件、气氛或声音
senses.example: The band recaptured the sound of the original record.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队再现了原版唱片的声音。
senses.why: Copying is another way of catching: the copy recaptures the original so closely that it is held again.
senses.whyCN: 复制也是「抓住」的一种：复制得足够像，就等于把原件重新握在手里。

senses.title: To get back what was paid or taken
senses.definition: to recover a cost or money through official or legal means
senses.definitionCN: 通过官方或法律手段追回成本或款项
senses.example: The council recaptured part of the cost through fees.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会通过收费追回了部分成本。
senses.why: In economics, recapture means reclaiming a benefit already given, a money version of catching back.
senses.whyCN: 在经济语境里，recapture 指收回已经给出的利益，是「抓回来」在金钱上的版本。

intro.en: Recapture combines the Latin prefix re-, again, with capture, which comes from Latin capere, to take. The Latin root is capt- from captus, the past participle of capere.
intro.cn: recapture 由拉丁语前缀 re-（再一次）与 capture 构成，capture 源于拉丁语 capere（抓取），词根 capt- 来自过去分词 captus。

items.en: Capere means to take, seize, or grasp.
items.cn: capere 意为拿、抓、握取。

items.en: Captus, the past participle, becomes the root capt- seen in capture and captor.
items.cn: 过去分词 captus 形成词根 capt-，见于 capture 与 captor。

items.en: Captura names a taking or a seizure, the direct ancestor of capture.
items.cn: captura 指抓取、夺取，是 capture 的直接祖先。

items.en: French capture keeps the noun meaning of a taking.
items.cn: 法语的 capture 保留「夺取」的名词含义。

items.en: English capture is first a noun and then a verb meaning to take by force.
items.cn: 英语 capture 先作名词，后作动词，意为以武力夺取。

items.en: Recapture is formed when re- is prefixed to capture, and it grows senses of feeling again and reproducing.
items.cn: recapture 是在 capture 前加词缀 re- 而成，并发展出「再次感受」与「再现」的义项。

note.en: Recapture is the re- word of the cap- family, next to capture, captor, and raptor, and it rubs shoulders with reclaim and retrieve.
note.cn: recapture 是 cap- 词族中带 re- 的词，与 capture、captor、raptor 同族，语义上靠近 reclaim 与 retrieve。

entries.definition: to take or catch someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 抓取；捕获；是 recapture 的基础动词

entries.definition: a person who takes another prisoner
entries.definitionCN: 同 capt- 词根，义为「俘获者；抓捕者」

entries.definition: a feeling of intense delight
entries.definitionCN: 同来自拉丁语抓取词根，原指「被抓住、被提走」，后转指「狂喜」

entries.definition: to get back something that is yours
entries.definitionCN: 取回；要回；多用于收回土地、财产或权利

entries.definition: to get something back from where it was left
entries.definitionCN: 取回；找回；强调从原处把东西拿回来

entries.definition: to get back something lost or taken
entries.definitionCN: 找回；恢复；最通用的「失而复得」

normalIntro.en: Recapture is capture done twice: the first grab failed, so the hand reaches out again.
normalIntro.cn: recapture 是「抓两次」的 capture：第一次没抓住，手又伸出去一次。

normal.en: Capture means to take, and re- means again, so recapture means to take back.
normal.cn: capture 是抓住，re- 是再一次，所以 recapture 是把人、地、感觉再抓回来。

normal.en: The noun recapture is usually uncountable, as in the recapture of the city.
normal.cn: 名词 recapture 通常不可数，如 the recapture of the city。

normal.en: You recapture a prisoner, a fort, a market, or a moment.
normal.cn: 宾语可以是囚犯、堡垒、市场，也可以是某个瞬间。

normal.en: The family also gives capture, captor, captive, and rapture.
normal.cn: 同族词还有 capture、captor、captive、rapture。

normal.en: Compare recover: recover is general, recapture stresses force or skill in taking back.
normal.cn: 对比 recover：recover 泛指失而复得，recapture 更强调用武力或技巧重新抓住。

abstract.en: Picture a bird fluttering away and a hand closing on it again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟扑棱着飞走，又被一只手一把攥住。

abstract.en: Imagine an army raising its flag again on a lost hill.
abstract.cn: 想象军队在失守的山头上重新升起旗帜。

abstract.en: Think of a photograph that brings a lost evening back in one glance.
abstract.cn: 想象一张照片让你一眼就找回那个失落的夜晚。

examples.en: The police recaptured the prisoner within a day.
examples.cn: 警方在一天之内重新抓获了那名囚犯。

examples.en: The novel recaptures the mood of a small town in the war years.
examples.cn: 这部小说重现了战争年代小镇的气氛。

examples.en: She hoped to recapture the confidence she had as a student.
examples.cn: 她希望能重新找回学生时代的那份自信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞卡普车」——瑞卡的车跑了，他又追上去把它抓回来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓取）→ 过去分词 captus → captura（夺取）→ 法语 capture → 英语 capture，加前缀 re-（再一次）得 recapture，核心义「再抓一次」。

sensesIntro.en: Recapture starts with catching an escaped thing, extends to taking back land and markets, and finally turns inward to reliving a feeling or reproducing an original.
sensesIntro.cn: recapture 从抓回逃跑之物开始，扩展到夺回土地与市场，最后转向内心，用来表达重温感受或再现原件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand seizing again what it once let go.
core.cn: 核心意象：手再一次抓住曾经放走的东西。

branches.en: Catching an escapee is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 抓住逃跑者是具体的身体义项。

branches.en: Taking back land and market share are both reversals of a loss.
branches.cn: 夺回土地与市场份额都是对「失去」的反转。

branches.en: Reliving a feeling is catching a moment that had slipped away.
branches.cn: 重温感受就是把已经溜走的瞬间再抓住。

branches.en: An accurate reproduction makes the past moment present again.
branches.cn: 准确的再现让过去的瞬间重新在场。

branches.en: Money recaptured is to resources what a fort recaptured is to a battlefield.
branches.cn: 追回款项之于资源，正如收复堡垒之于战场。

intro.en: Recapture joins the Latin prefix re- to capture, so its family runs through capere, captus, and captura, and through English words such as captor and captive.
intro.cn: recapture 由拉丁语前缀 re- 加在 capture 上构成，其词族贯穿 capere、captus、captura，以及英语的 captor、captive 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere means to take, and its participle captus supplies the capt- root seen across capture, captor, captive, and rapture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取，其分词 captus 提供 capt- 词根，见于 capture、captor、captive、rapture 等词。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the idea of doing the action again.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示把动作再做一遍。

items.example: The root capt- carries the idea of seizing.
items.exampleCN: 词根 capt- 承载「抓取」的意思。

items.example: Capere is the Latin verb behind capture.
items.exampleCN: capere 是 capture 背后的拉丁语动词。

items.example: Captura becomes capture in English.
items.exampleCN: captura 在英语中演变成 capture。

items.example: The suffix -ure forms capture.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ure 构成 capture。

items.example: Captor shares the seizing root with capture.
items.exampleCN: captor 与 capture 共享「抓取」词根。

items.example: Captive describes someone who has been taken.
items.exampleCN: captive 描述被抓住、被关起来的人。

items.example: Captivate extends the seizing image to attention.
items.exampleCN: captivate 把「抓住」的意象扩展到注意力上。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms recaptured.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 recaptured。

latinEntries.example: Capere gives the core image of seizing.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 提供「抓取」的核心意象。
captus 提供 capt- 词根。

latinEntries.example: Captura is the direct ancestor of capture.
latinEntries.exampleCN: captura 是 capture 的直接祖先。

latinEntries.example: Latin re- matches the prefix in recapture.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 re- 与 recapture 的前缀一致。

definition_zh: 接待员；前台；挂号员
definition_en: a person whose job is to greet visitors, answer the telephone, and deal with enquiries at the entrance of an office, hotel, or clinic
core_image: 进门第一张桌子后面坐着的那个人，抬头问你找谁
scene: 酒店门口，一位穿制服的接待员微笑着接过客人的身份证，问对方有没有预订。At the hotel entrance, the receptionist smiles and asks the guest whether he has a reservation.
sceneCN: 这里 receptionist 是「接待员」（第 1 个义项：在前厅迎接来访者的工作人员）；句意：酒店门口，接待员微笑着问客人是否有预订。

pos.zh: 接待员；（酒店、诊所的）前台；挂号员

derivatives.zh: receive 加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「接待；接待处」，是 receptionist 的词干
心理学与哲学术语，义为「接受性；感受」，由 receive 的过去分词词干 recept- 加零后缀构成
recept- 加形容词后缀 -ive，义为「易于接受的；善于领会的」
由 reception 加 desk 构成的合成名词，义为「接待台；前台」

senses.title: The person who greets visitors at the front desk
senses.definition: an employee posted at the entrance of an office, hotel, or other building to welcome callers and direct them onward
senses.definitionCN: 受派在办公楼、酒店等单位入口迎接来访者并指引方向的员工
senses.example: Please report to the receptionist when you arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 您到达后请先到前台登记。
senses.why: The job name is built on reception, the act of receiving guests, plus the agent suffix -ist, so the word literally means the person who does the receiving.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「接待」的 reception 加上施事后缀 -ist 构成，字面就是「负责接待的那个人」；核心意象里第一个被看见的人，正是这个角色。

senses.title: The staff member who answers the phone and handles bookings
senses.definition: a front desk employee who takes incoming calls, handles reservations, and passes messages on
senses.definitionCN: 负责接听来电、办理预订并转达留言的前台员工
senses.example: The receptionist booked us a table for eight.
senses.exampleCN: 前台帮我们订了一张八人桌。
senses.why: The same desk receives both footsteps and telephone calls, so the person at it takes the bookings and messages as well.
senses.whyCN: 同一张前台桌子接收的不只是脚步声，还有电话声，因此接待员也承担订位与留言的职责，这是从「迎客」自然延伸出来的第二层。

senses.title: A hospital or clinic clerk who registers patients
senses.definition: a clerk at a hospital or clinic who registers patients and arranges their appointments
senses.definitionCN: 在医院或诊所给病人登记、安排就诊的职员
senses.example: The receptionist asked for my insurance card and gave me a form.
senses.exampleCN: 挂号员要了我的医保卡，又递给我一张表格。
senses.why: In British hospitals the front desk is called reception and its clerk a receptionist, so the word covers non-guest settings too.
senses.whyCN: 英式医疗语境里医院前台也叫 reception，它的职员便叫 receptionist，于是这个词也用在非宾客的场所，专指挂号登记的人。

senses.title: An entry-level front desk post
senses.definition: a job title for the position itself, often a first rung on a career ladder
senses.definitionCN: 作为职位名使用，常是职业路径的第一级台阶
senses.example: She started as a receptionist and is now the office manager.
senses.exampleCN: 她从前台做起，现在是办公室经理了。
senses.why: Because the post requires little seniority, the word is often used for a stepping stone rather than a career.
senses.whyCN: 这个职位门槛不高，于是词义常带「起点」色彩：不只是某个人，而是某条职业道路的第一站。

senses.title: The face of an organisation
senses.definition: used figuratively for the first point of contact that shapes a visitor first impression of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指塑造访客对机构第一印象的第一个接触点
senses.example: In many firms the receptionist is the public face of the whole company.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多公司里，接待员就是整家公司的对外门面。
senses.why: The core image puts this person at the doorway, so the word can summarise the whole threshold experience of a company.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象把这个人放在门口，所以这个词能用来概括一家公司的全部门口体验，比喻成「门面」。

intro.en: Receptionist is an English formation of the nineteenth century: reception comes from Latin recepio via Old French, and -ist was added to name the person.
intro.cn: receptionist 是英语自身构成的词，十九世纪出现：reception 经由古法语来自拉丁语 recipere 的派生名词，再在词尾加 -ist 指名「人」。

items.en: Recipere means to take back or receive, from re- back plus capere to take.
items.cn: 拉丁语 recipere 意为「收回；接收」，由 re-（向后）与 capere（拿取）合成。

items.en: The derived noun receptio names the act of receiving.
items.cn: 派生名词 receptio 表示「接收、接待」这一行为。

items.en: The noun passes into Old French as reception, meaning the act of receiving a guest.
items.cn: 该名词进入古法语作 reception，意为接待宾客。

items.en: Middle English reception covers both the formal welcome of a guest and the act of taking something in.
items.cn: 中古英语 reception 同时指正式迎宾和接收事物。

items.en: The agent suffix -ist is added to reception, giving receptionist for the person who receives callers.
items.cn: 十九世纪在 reception 后加施事后缀 -ist，构成 receptionist，指负责接待来访者的人。

items.en: As offices, hotels, and clinics grew, the word became a standard job title across them.
items.cn: 随着办公楼、酒店和诊所的增多，该词成为这些场所通用的职位名称。

note.en: Receptionist belongs to the receive family and sits in the same field as clerk, usher, and other front desk roles.
note.cn: receptionist 属于 receive 家族，与 clerk、usher 等前台角色同处一个义场。

entries.definition: the desk area where guests are received
entries.definitionCN: 接待处；前台，是 receptionist 的词干

entries.definition: willing to listen to or accept new ideas
entries.definitionCN: 乐于接受新想法的，与 receptionist 同出 receive 一词

entries.definition: a written proof that money or goods were received
entries.definitionCN: 收据，同出拉丁语 recipere，指收到的凭据

entries.definition: a person who does office or counter work, such as answering questions or keeping records
entries.definitionCN: 职员；柜台办事员，与接待员职责有重叠

entries.definition: a person who shows people to their seats at an event
entries.definitionCN: 引座员，负责把客人带到座位上

entries.definition: a hotel employee who arranges services for guests
entries.definitionCN: 酒店礼宾员，负责为客人安排各类服务

normalIntro.en: Receptionist is reception plus -ist, so think of the person whose whole job is the act of receiving.
normalIntro.cn: receptionist 就是 reception 加 -ist，记住「专职做接待的那个人」。

normal.en: The suffix -ist usually marks a person, as in artist, dentist, and journalist.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ist 通常表示人，如 artist、dentist、journalist。

normal.en: Reception is literally the desk or room for receiving guests, so the receptionist is the person who works there.
normal.cn: reception 字面就是「接待宾客的地方」，所以 receptionist 是在那儿工作的人。

normal.en: The verb receive is hidden in the stem: to receive a guest is to play host.
normal.cn: 词干里藏着动词 receive：接收客人就是在做主人。

normal.en: In British English the desk is often just called reception, and the job title is built on it.
normal.cn: 英式英语里前台常简称为 reception，职位名就由此而来。

normal.en: Compare reception with receipt: both come from Latin recipere, to take back.
normal.cn: 对比 reception 与 receipt：二者都来自拉丁语 recipere，意为「收回、接收」。

abstract.en: Picture a person seated behind the first desk you see in any hotel.
abstract.cn: 想象任何人一进酒店就看见的第一张桌子后面坐着的那个人。

abstract.en: Hear a ringing telephone at the desk being lifted before the second ring.
abstract.cn: 听见前台电话在第二声铃响前就被接起。

abstract.en: Imagine a small queue of patients waiting while the clerk looks up a name on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象几位病人在排队，登记员在屏幕上查名字。

examples.en: The receptionist handed me a visitor badge and pointed to the lift.
examples.cn: 前台递给我一张访客证，并指了指电梯。

examples.en: We phoned the receptionist to change our room, and she arranged it at once.
examples.cn: 我们打电话给前台换了房间，她立刻就办好了。

examples.en: A polite receptionist can make a difficult complaint much easier to handle.
examples.cn: 一位有礼貌的接待员能让棘手的投诉好处理得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞塞普逊尼斯特」——太长了，只记前两段「瑞塞普」，谐音「睿瑟谱」：前台要沉着睿智、办事有谱。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后、回来）+ capere（拿取）→ recipere（接收）→ receptio（接收、接待）→ 古法语 reception → 英语 reception + 施事后缀 -ist → receptionist（接待员）。

sensesIntro.en: Receptionist starts as the person at the front desk, widens to cover phone and booking work, then hospital registration, the job title itself, and finally the figurative face of an organisation.
sensesIntro.cn: receptionist 先指前台迎客的人，再扩展到接电话与订位的工作，然后是医院挂号，进而用作职位名，最后比喻为机构的门面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person behind the first desk, looking up and asking whom you have come to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：进门第一张桌子后面的人，抬头问你来访找谁。

branches.en: Greeting and directing visitors is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 迎接并指引来访者是最基本的字面义项。

branches.en: Phone work and patient registration extend the same desk to other kinds of receiving.
branches.cn: 接电话与病人挂号把同一张桌子延伸到别的「接收」场景。

branches.en: As a job title the word names an entry-level post.
branches.cn: 作职位名时，它指入门级的岗位。

branches.en: The figurative face of a company grows out of the doorway image.
branches.cn: 「机构门面」的比喻义由门口意象生长出来。

branches.en: The receptionist both welcomes visitors and represents the institution to them.
branches.cn: 接待员既迎接访客，也代表机构与访客打交道。

intro.en: Receptionist is built from the Latin verb recipere through the noun reception, with the English agent suffix -ist added at the end.
intro.cn: receptionist 由拉丁语动词 recipere 经由名词 reception 一层层构成，最后加上英语施事后缀 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin recipere joins re-, back, with capere, to take, giving the sense of taking something in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 recipere 由 re-（向后）与 capere（拿取）组合，取得「收进来」的意思。

items.example: Recept- is the past participle stem of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: recept- 是拉丁语动词的过去分词词干。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion turns a verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成表示行为的名词。

items.meaning: the act of receiving guests, or the desk where it happens
items.example: Guests were asked to wait at reception.
items.exampleCN: 客人被请在前台等候。

items.meaning: a person who does or practises something
items.meaningCN: 表示从事某活动的人的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ist marks the person, as in artist or dentist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 标记「人」，如 artist、dentist。

items.example: The receptionist keeps the visitor list.
items.exampleCN: 接待员保管访客登记表。

items.meaningCN: 表示具有某种倾向的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms receptive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 receptive。

items.meaningCN: 乐于接受的；善于领会的
items.example: Students were receptive to the new approach.
items.exampleCN: 学生们乐于接受新方法。

items.example: The prefix con- with capere gives concept, a thing taken together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 与 capere 组合成 concept，意为「一并把握的东西」。

items.meaning: a person who does an action
items.meaningCN: 表示「做某事的人」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er is the rival of -ist in forming job names.
items.exampleCN: 在构成职位名时，后缀 -er 是 -ist 的另一常见选择。

definition_zh: 休息；课间休息；暂停；凹进处；使休会
definition_en: a short break in the working day or in a formal meeting, or a hollow part set back from the main surface
core_image: 一堵墙往里凹进去一块，正好能站下一个人躲太阳
scene: 课间休息的钟声一响，孩子们冲出教室，跑到操场上追逐。When the bell for recess rang, the children rushed out of the classroom and ran across the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 recess 是「休息；课间休息」（第 1 个义项：工作中或课间的一次短暂中止）；句意：课间铃一响，孩子们冲出教室跑到操场上。

pos.zh: 休息；课间休息；休会期；凹进处；深处
使休会；暂停；把……放在凹处

derivatives.zh: recess 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，本义「后退」，现代指经济衰退
recess- 加形容词后缀 -ive，义为「隐性遗传的；后退的」
过去分词转化为形容词，义为「嵌入式的；凹进去的」
recession 加形容词后缀 -al，义为「退场的」，常用于教堂礼拜结束的退场圣歌

senses.title: A short break during work or school
senses.definition: a short period when classes, work, or activity stops so that people can rest before it begins again
senses.definitionCN: 课堂、工作或活动暂停的一小段时间，让人们休息后再继续
senses.example: The pupils play tag at recess every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们每天早上课间都玩抓人游戏。
senses.why: Latin recessus means a going back, and a break is a step back from the task, so the hollow image becomes a pause in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recessus 意为「往回走」，休息就是从手头的事里退开一步；核心意象里的「凹陷」于是转到时间上，变成一段陷进去的空当。

senses.title: A formal suspension of a meeting or court
senses.definition: a planned pause in a parliament, court, or conference before business resumes
senses.definitionCN: 议会、法庭或会议在继续议事前的有计划的中止
senses.example: The judge called a brief recess before the next witness.
senses.exampleCN: 在下一位证人出庭前，法官宣布短暂休庭。
senses.why: A formal body also steps back from the matter at hand, so the same word names an official interval in a court or chamber.
senses.whyCN: 正式机构同样需要从议题前退开，于是这个词又指法庭或议会的正式间歇，与课间休息同出一源。

senses.title: A long seasonal break for a governing body
senses.definition: the long period in the year when a legislature or court does not sit
senses.definitionCN: 立法机关或法院一年中不开庭、不开会的较长期间
senses.example: Parliament is in recess until September.
senses.exampleCN: 议会休会到九月。
senses.why: The short pause lengthens into a season, so the word names the gap between sessions rather than a single interval.
senses.whyCN: 短暂的停顿拉长成整个季节，所以这个词也指两届会期之间的整段空白，而非一次间歇。

senses.title: A hollow niche set back in a surface
senses.definition: a part of a wall or surface that is set back, often used as a shelf or alcove
senses.definitionCN: 墙面或其他表面上向内退进的一块，常用作搁架或小龛
senses.example: Candles stood in a narrow recess beside the altar.
senses.exampleCN: 祭坛旁边一个狭窄的凹处里立着蜡烛。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most physical sense: a space that has gone back, exactly matching the core image.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最具体的义项：朝里退进去的一块空间，与核心意象完全吻合，是整条语义链的起点。

senses.title: The inner depths of a place or a process
senses.definition: the deepest or least visible parts of a place, a mind, or a system
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、头脑或体系中最深、最不易看见的部分
senses.example: The law is hidden in the recesses of bureaucratic memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这条法律藏在官僚记忆的最深处。
senses.why: Hollows are the places where things are tucked away, so the plural recesses means hidden inner corners.
senses.whyCN: 凹处正是东西被塞进去的地方，因此复数 recesses 常指隐秘的内心深处或角落。

senses.title: To break off a meeting temporarily
senses.definition: to stop a meeting or court for a short time and resume it later
senses.definitionCN: 把会议或庭审短暂停止，稍后再继续
senses.example: The chair recessed the session until ten tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 主席宣布会议暂停，明天十点继续。
senses.why: From the noun comes a verb: to impose a going back on a meeting is to recess it.
senses.whyCN: 名词之外又长出动词：把「往回退」施加到会议身上，就是使会议休会，这是词性转移带来的义项。

intro.en: Recess follows Latin recessus, a going back, through the Latin verb recedere.
intro.cn: recess 经由拉丁语动词 recedere 及其名词 recessus（后退），进入英语。

items.en: Recedere means to go back or withdraw, from re- back plus cedere to go.
items.cn: 拉丁语 recedere 意为「退回；退出」，由 re-（向后）与 cedere（走）合成。

items.en: The noun recessus names a going back, and also a backward space such as a bay or inlet.
items.cn: 名词 recessus 表示「后退」这一动作，也指向内退入的一处空间，如海湾。

items.en: In church and legal Latin recessus also names a formal withdrawal from a sitting or session.
items.cn: 在教会与法律拉丁语中，recessus 也指正式退出一次开庭或集会。

items.en: English first uses recess for a hidden or remote place and for the act of withdrawing.
items.cn: 英语最初用 recess 指幽深隐蔽之处以及退出的行为。

items.en: The sense of a pause in court or parliament is recorded, and later a school break.
items.cn: 「法庭或议会暂停」的义项见于记载，其后又出现「学校课间休息」的用法。

items.en: American usage makes recess the ordinary word for a school playtime.
items.cn: 美式用法使 recess 成为学校课间休息的日常用词。

note.en: Recess belongs to the Latin cedere family of going and yielding, and to the everyday field of breaks.
note.cn: recess 属于拉丁语 cedere（走开）家族，也处在「休息、中断」这一日常义场中。

entries.definition: a period when trade and industry shrink and jobs are lost
entries.definitionCN: 经济衰退，与 recess 同出「后退」之义

entries.definition: to move back, as flood water does
to go on after a pause
entries.definitionCN: 前行；继续进行，与 recess 共享 cedere 词根但意思相反

entries.definition: a short rest between periods of work
entries.definitionCN: 休息，最普通的中断用词

entries.definition: a period of time between two events or parts of a performance
to stop a meeting and continue it at another time
entries.definitionCN: 休会；延期，多用于会议与法庭

normalIntro.en: Recess is a going back in Latin: the word puts your back to the wall, then lets the wall become the gap in time.
normalIntro.cn: recess 在拉丁语里是「往回走」：先把后背靠进墙里，再让墙上的凹陷变成时间里的空当。

normal.en: The prefix re- means back, as in return, retreat, and recede.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「向后」，如 return、retreat、recede。

normal.en: The root ced means to go, seen in proceed and exceed.
normal.cn: 词根 ced 表示「走」，见于 proceed 与 exceed。

normal.en: So recess is a going back: going back from a lesson is a break, going back into a wall is an alcove.
normal.cn: 所以 recess 就是往回走：从课上退开是休息，退进墙里就是壁龛。

normal.en: Recession shares the going back image and became the word for the economy shrinking back.
normal.cn: recession 同样带着「后退」的形象，后来成了经济缩退的说法。

normal.en: In court and parliament the chair may declare a recess, and in American schools the bell marks recess.
normal.cn: 法庭和议会里主持人可以宣布休会，美式学校则用铃声标记课间。

abstract.en: Picture the din of a corridor suddenly falling silent as the bell frees everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象铃声一响，走廊的喧闹忽然散开，所有人都被放了出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a judge laying down the pen and standing up to wait outside the room.
abstract.cn: 想象法官放下笔，起身走到房间外等候。

abstract.en: Think of a stone alcove in a thick stone wall, a space carved out of the wall itself.
abstract.cn: 想象厚石墙里挖出的一个石龛，那是墙本身让出来的一小块空间。

examples.en: The children get twenty minutes of recess after their second lesson.
examples.cn: 孩子们上完第二节课后有二十分钟的课间休息。

examples.en: Negotiations were in recess for the whole of August.
examples.cn: 整个八月谈判都处于暂停状态。

examples.en: A small recess in the wall held the family photographs.
examples.cn: 墙上一个小凹处放着全家的照片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞塞斯」——课间一到，大家都把自己「塞」进休息里，教室被「塞」得空空的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ cedere（走）→ recedere（退回）→ recessus（后退；凹处）→ 古法语 recess → 英语 recess，核心义「往回退进去的空当」。

sensesIntro.en: Recess begins as a hollow set back in a surface, then becomes a pause in time, an official suspension, a seasonal gap, a hidden depth, and finally a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: recess 起于空间中向内退进的一块，再转为时间上的中止，发展为正式的休会、整季的休会期、隐秘的深处，最后作动词使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hollow pushed back into a wall, a place where a person can step aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙里向内退进去的一个凹处，是人可以退到一边的地方。

branches.en: A short break is the going back applied to daily routine.
branches.cn: 短暂休息是把「退回」用在日常作息上。

branches.en: The formal suspension and its verb keep the institutional sense.
branches.cn: 正式休庭休会及其动词用法保留了机构层面的含义。

branches.en: The seasonal gap stretches the pause into months.
branches.cn: 季节休会期把停顿拉长到好几个月。

branches.en: The physical alcove is the source image of the whole family.
branches.cn: 具体的壁龛是整个词义家族的源头意象。

branches.en: Hidden depths are alcoves in a place or a mind.
branches.cn: 深处就是一个地方或一颗心里的壁龛。

intro.en: Recess is built on Latin cedere, to go, with the prefix re-, back, and a noun ending; English then forms recession, recede, and recessed from it.
intro.cn: recess 由拉丁语 cedere（走）加前缀 re-（向后）和名词词尾构成，英语再由此形成 recession、recede、recessed。

latinIntro.en: Latin recedere means to go back, and its noun recessus gives both the act of withdrawing and the space left behind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 recedere 意为退回，其名词 recessus 既指退出的动作，也指退出来留下的空间。

items.example: The prefix re- in recedere points backwards.
items.exampleCN: recedere 中的前缀 re- 指向后方。

items.example: The root ced- appears in cedere, to go.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ced- 见于 cedere，意为「走」。

items.meaningCN: 拉丁语第四变格法名词词尾
items.example: The ending -us makes recessus a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -us 把 recessus 变成动作名词。

items.meaning: a break, a hollow; to suspend
items.example: Recess keeps both the spatial and the temporal senses.
items.exampleCN: recess 同时保留空间义与时间义。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion carries recess into recession.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把 recess 发展为 recession。

items.meaning: a shrinking back of trade and output
items.example: A recession followed the collapse in demand.
items.exampleCN: 需求崩塌之后出现了经济衰退。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms recessive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 recessive。

items.meaning: having been acted on, or having a stated feature
items.meaningCN: 表示「已被……的」或「具有某种特征的」后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed forms recessed, set back into a surface.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 recessed，指嵌进表面里的。

items.example: The prefix ex- with cedere gives exceed.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 与 cedere 构成 exceed。

definition_zh: 惯犯；累犯；屡教不改者
definition_en: a person who keeps returning to criminal behaviour after being punished, or who relapses into any bad habit
core_image: 又回到那道已经跨过的大门前的脚印，一圈一圈叠在第一个人留下的痕上
scene: 法官看着被告的档案，这已经是他第三次因盗窃被判刑，于是法庭把他定为惯犯。The judge studied the file and saw a third conviction for theft, so the court classed him as a recidivist.
sceneCN: 这里 recidivist 是「惯犯」（第 1 个义项：受罚之后再次犯罪的人）；句意：法官见被告已是第三次因盗窃被判刑，便将其定为惯犯。

pos.zh: 惯犯；累犯；屡教不改者；复发者
惯犯的；累犯的；屡次复发的

derivatives.zh: recidivist 的词干加抽象名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「累犯；屡犯倾向」
recidivist 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「累犯倾向的」
从法语同源词借入的罕见动词，义为「复发；再犯」

senses.title: A criminal who offends again after punishment
senses.definition: a person who returns to crime after being convicted or punished, especially one who does so repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 被定罪或处罚后再次犯罪的人，尤指一犯再犯的人
senses.example: The court treated him as a recidivist and refused bail.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把他当作惯犯，拒绝予以保释。
senses.why: Latin recidivus means falling back, and -ist marks a person, so a recidivist is literally one who falls back into the deed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recidivus 意为「往回倒」，-ist 标记「人」，所以 recidivist 字面就是「又倒回去做那件事的人」；核心意象里叠起的脚印正是这种反复。

senses.title: A person who relapses into a disease or habit
senses.definition: a patient or drinker who suffers an illness or bad habit again after a period of recovery
senses.definitionCN: 在痊愈一段时间后旧病复发或重新沉溺于恶习的病人、酗酒者
senses.example: Many recidivists relapse in the first month after treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 很多康复者会在治疗后的第一个月旧病复发。
senses.why: Medicine took over the legal word: the same falling back happens in a body or a habit as in a criminal record.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个法律词：同一种「往回倒」既发生在犯罪记录里，也发生在身体或恶习里，于是它泛指复发者。

senses.title: The descriptive adjective recidivist
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe behaviour, tendencies, or persons that keep returning to an offence
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，描述屡次回到同一错误、罪行的行为、倾向或人
senses.example: Recidivist behaviour is often shaped by the conditions of the prison.
senses.exampleCN: 累犯行为往往由监狱环境所塑造。
senses.why: English allows the same word as a modifier, so the person noun also describes the pattern that defines the person.
senses.whyCN: 英语里同一词形可作定语，于是这个指人的名词也能描述那种定义此人的「反复」模式。

senses.title: Anyone who falls back into an old bad pattern
senses.titleCN: 屡教不改的人；故态复萌者
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who keeps breaking the same promise, diet, or rule despite resolutions
senses.definitionCN: 引申指反复打破同一个承诺、节食计划或规矩，屡教不改的人
senses.example: As a recidivist dieter, he starts again every January.
senses.exampleCN: 作为一个屡教不改的节食者，他每年一月都重新开始。
senses.why: Once the medical sense loosens the legal frame, the word can point at any habit that keeps coming back.
senses.whyCN: 医学义项松动法律框架之后，这个词便能指向任何反复回来纠缠人的习惯，成为一般性的幽默说法。

senses.title: A repeat offender in regulation or sport
senses.definition: a person or team that repeatedly breaks a rule, a boundary, or a limit set by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 反复违反当局规定、界限或限额的个人或团队
senses.example: The airline is a recidivist on the noise league table.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司在噪音排行榜上是屡犯者。
