senses.why: Regulators apply the criminal pattern to institutions, so a firm that keeps breaching the rules can be a recidivist too.
senses.whyCN: 监管者把犯罪模式套到机构身上，因此屡次违规的公司也可以叫 recidivist，这是法律义的行业化平移。

intro.en: Recidivist comes from Latin recidivus, falling back, formed on cadere, to fall, with the prefix re-.
intro.cn: recidivist 来自拉丁语 recidivus（再度落回的），由前缀 re- 与 cadere（落下）构成。

items.en: Cadere means to fall, and with re- the verb recidere means to fall back.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为「落下」，加上 re- 后 recidere 表示「落回」。

items.en: The adjective recidivus describes something that falls back or returns to an earlier state.
items.cn: 形容词 recidivus 描述「落回原状、退回先前状态」的事物。

items.en: French récidiviste names a repeat offender in legal usage.
items.cn: 十九世纪法语 récidiviste 在法律语境中指名累犯。

items.en: English borrows recidivist in the nineteenth century, chiefly as a legal term.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入 recidivist，主要用作法律术语。

items.en: Criminology, psychiatry, and public health spread recidivism and recidivist beyond the courtroom.
items.cn: 犯罪学、精神病学与公共卫生把 recidivism、recidivist 从法庭推向更广的领域。

items.en: Today the word also describes any repeated relapse into a bad habit.
items.cn: 如今这个词也泛指对任何恶习的反复复发。

note.en: Recidivist belongs to the Latin cadere family of falling and to the legal field of repeat offenders.
note.cn: recidivist 属于拉丁语 cadere（落下）家族，也处在「屡犯者」这一法律义场中。

entries.definition: the tendency of a punished person to offend again
entries.definitionCN: 累犯倾向，是 recidivist 的抽象名词

entries.definition: the rate at which something, especially disease, occurs
entries.definitionCN: 发生率，只是与 recidivist 共享 cad- 词根，词源同源而意义不同

entries.definition: the measured fall and rise of rhythm in speech or music
entries.definitionCN: 节奏；韵律，同出拉丁语 cadere（落下），但指声音的落点

entries.definition: a person who breaks the law
entries.definitionCN: 违法者；罪犯，不强调是否再犯

entries.definition: a person who cannot stop using a substance or habit
entries.definitionCN: 成瘾者，与「复发」义项最为接近

entries.definition: a person who falls back into old bad ways
entries.definitionCN: 故态复萌者，语体比 recidivist 更轻

normalIntro.en: Recidivist is Latin re-, back, plus cadere, to fall, plus -ist, a person: the one who falls back.
normalIntro.cn: recidivist 是拉丁语 re-（向后）+ cadere（落下）+ -ist（人）的合成：一个又落回去的人。

normal.en: The root cad means to fall, as in decay and accident, a thing that happens to fall.
normal.cn: 词根 cad 表示「落下」，如 decay 与 accident（偶然落下的事）。

normal.en: Recidivism turns the person into the tendency, so the -ism ending means the pattern, not the man.
normal.cn: recidivism 把「人」换成「倾向」，-ism 词尾表示的是模式而非人。

normal.en: Latin recidivus is a slipping back, the same image as a wound that reopens.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 recidivus 是「滑落回去」，与伤口重新裂开是同一个画面。

normal.en: The French legal form récidiviste came before the English word, so think first of a court and a file.
normal.cn: 英语词源自法语法律用语 récidiviste，所以先想到法庭和一个人的卷宗。

normal.en: Recidivist is a formal word; in plain speech say repeat offender or repeat drinker.
normal.cn: recidivist 很正式，口语里说重复犯罪的、反复酗酒的更自然。

abstract.en: Picture footprints that keep returning to the same prison gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一串脚印一次次回到同一道监狱大门前。

abstract.en: Imagine a wound that closes and then splits again in exactly the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一道伤口愈合后又在同一位置裂开。

abstract.en: Think of a person who writes the same apology note for the third time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人第三次写下同一封道歉信。

examples.en: The study found that half of the released prisoners became recidivists within two years.
examples.cn: 研究发现，获释的犯人中有一半在两年内成了累犯。

examples.en: As a recidivist offender, he faced a longer sentence than a first-time thief.
examples.cn: 作为累犯，他面临的刑期比初犯者更长。

examples.en: The report names the company as a recidivist polluter.
examples.cn: 报告点名这家公司是屡次违规的排污者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞西迪维斯特」——把它拆成「瑞西·迪维斯特」，谐音「惹西边、敌维斯特」：总是回到老地方去惹事，正是惯犯；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ cadere（落下）→ recidere（落回）→ recidivus（再度落回的）→ 法语 récidiviste → 英语 recidivist（惯犯），核心义「又跌回原处」。

sensesIntro.en: Recidivist begins with the legal repeat offender, spreads to medical relapse and the descriptive adjective, then to any stubborn habit and finally to repeat violations by organisations.
sensesIntro.cn: recidivist 起于法律上的累犯，扩展到旧病复发者与形容词用法，再泛指任何屡教不改的恶习，最后用于机构屡次违规。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footprints that keep coming back to the place they were meant to leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚印一次次回到本该离开的地方。

branches.en: The repeat offender is the founding legal sense.
branches.cn: 累犯是这个词最初的法律义项。

branches.en: Medical relapse borrows the falling back for the body.
branches.cn: 医学上的复发把「往回倒」借给了身体。

branches.en: The adjective use lets the same word describe the pattern.
branches.cn: 形容词用法让同一词形去描述这种反复模式。

branches.en: Any stubborn habit can be a recidivist pattern in daily speech.
branches.cn: 在日常口语里，任何屡教不改的习惯都可用这个词形容。

branches.en: Institutions that keep breaking rules are judged in criminal terms.
branches.cn: 屡次违规的机构被用犯罪的语言来评判。

intro.en: Recidivist is assembled from the Latin prefix re-, the root cad-, and the agent suffix -ist; the modern family adds -ism and -istic.
intro.cn: recidivist 由拉丁语前缀 re-、词根 cad- 和施事后缀 -ist 拼成，现代英语再补上 -ism 与 -istic 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere means to fall, and recidere, its compound with re-, means to fall back or relapse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为落下，与 re- 合成的 recidere 意为落回、复发。

items.example: The prefix re- doubles the falling back into a return.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把落下变成再一次落回。

items.example: The root cad- sits inside cadere, to fall.
items.exampleCN: 词根 cad- 就藏在 cadere（落下）里。

items.meaningCN: 具有某种性质的构词成分
items.example: The element -iv- makes recidivus an adjective of tendency.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -iv- 使 recidivus 成为表示倾向的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ist turns the falling back into a person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 把「落回」变成一个人。

items.example: The recidivist was denied bail.
items.exampleCN: 这名惯犯未获保释。

items.meaningCN: 表示做法或倾向的抽象名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms recidivism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 recidivism。

items.example: Recidivism fell after the education programme began.
items.exampleCN: 教育项目实施后，累犯率下降了。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms recidivistic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 recidivistic。

items.example: The prefix de- with cad- gives decadence, a falling down.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 与 cad- 构成 decadence，意为「衰落」。

definition_zh: 回报；报答；回应（感情、善意）；做双向互动的动作；使（机器部件）往复运动；互惠
definition_en: to return a feeling, favour, or action in kind, to move back and forth, or to make a part move back and forth
core_image: 两只手一推一送，一股力送出去又沿原路折返回来
scene: 邻居送来一篮自己种的番茄，收下的人隔天回赠一瓶果酱。When a neighbour brought a basket of tomatoes, she baked a jar of jam to reciprocate.
sceneCN: 这里 reciprocate 是「回报」（第 1 个义项：以同样的行动回应别人的好意）；句意：邻居送来一篮番茄，她就烤了一罐果酱作为回礼。

pos.zh: 回报；报答；回应（感情、善意）；互惠
以同样方式回应；交换（问候、礼节）；使往复运动

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「回报；互惠；往复运动」
由拉丁词根构成，义为「相互的；互惠的」，数学里也指「倒数」
形容词 reciprocal 加 -ity 构成，义为「互惠；对等；礼尚往来」
现在分词作定语，义为「往复式的」，如 reciprocating saw（往复锯）

senses.title: To return a kindness in kind
senses.definition: to do something helpful for someone who has helped you, usually in the same way or to a similar degree
senses.definitionCN: 对帮助过自己的人做同样的好事，通常方式相同或程度相当
senses.example: She baked a cake to reciprocate his help with the move.
senses.exampleCN: 他帮她搬了家，她就烤了个蛋糕作为答谢。
senses.why: Latin reciprocus describes a movement that returns to where it started, so a kind act comes back to the giver along the same path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 reciprocus 指「回到原处」的运动，所以善意沿着同一条路回到施予者身上，这就是回报。

senses.title: To return a feeling or gesture
senses.definition: to show the same emotion or greeting towards someone that they have shown to you
senses.definitionCN: 用对方给过的同一份情感或礼节来回敬对方
senses.example: He smiled at her, and she reciprocated with a nod.
senses.exampleCN: 他冲她笑了笑，她以点头回应。
senses.why: The back and forth image fits feelings and greetings too: a smile arrives, a smile goes back.
senses.whyCN: 一来一回的意象同样适用于情感与寒暄：一个微笑递过来，另一个微笑送回去。

senses.title: To move back and forth
senses.definition: to move backwards and forwards in a regular way, or to make a part move like this
senses.definitionCN: 有规律地来回移动，或使某个部件这样来回运动
senses.example: The piston reciprocates inside the cylinder.
senses.exampleCN: 活塞在气缸里做往复运动。
senses.why: This is the oldest mechanical sense: the piston comes back along the same line it went forward on.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的机械义：活塞沿着去的那条直线再回来，正是「折返」的原始画面。

senses.title: An exchange of equal value
senses.definition: to exchange ideas, rights, or benefits so that both sides give and receive
senses.definitionCN: 交换思想、权利或利益，使双方都有给有得
senses.example: The two universities reciprocate research grants each year.
senses.exampleCN: 两所大学每年互给对方提供研究经费。
senses.why: When the returning movement happens on both sides at once, the result is a two way exchange rather than one sided giving.
senses.whyCN: 当双方的折返同时发生，单方面的给予就变成双向的交换，这是现代谈判与外交里的常用义。

intro.en: Reciprocate comes from Latin reciprocus, moving back and forth, and through the Latin verb reciprocare, to cause to move back.
intro.cn: reciprocate 来自拉丁语 reciprocus（来回移动的），经由拉丁语动词 reciprocare（使回到原处）进入英语。

items.en: The form reciprocus describes a motion that returns along the same path, while the adverb suggests doing a thing in turn; the exact make-up of the form is unclear, and it is often glossed as going back the way one came.
items.cn: 拉丁语形式 reciprocus 描述沿原路折返的运动，副词则略带「轮流、反过来」之意；其构词成分的来历已不易确定，一般认为取「沿原来路径返回」之意。

items.en: Reciprocare, to make something move back, becomes a verb in classical Latin.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语中出现了动词 reciprocare，意为「使某物折返」。

items.en: Church and legal Latin use reciprocus for things exchanged in turn, such as mutual goodwill.
items.cn: 教会与法律拉丁语用 reciprocus 指轮流交换的事物，如相互的善意。

items.en: The English verb is recorded in the sixteenth century, first for alternating movement and exchange.
items.cn: 英语动词在十六世纪见诸记载，起初指交替运动与相互交换。

items.en: With the rise of machines, reciprocating comes to describe the up and down or back and forth stroke of a piston.
items.cn: 随着机械兴起，reciprocating 用来描述活塞上下或前后的冲程。

items.en: In modern English the social sense, returning a kindness or a feeling, is the most frequent.
items.cn: 现代英语中最常用的是社交义：回报恩情、回应感情。

note.en: Reciprocate shares its stem with reciprocal and reciprocity, and is close in meaning to return, repay, and exchange.
note.cn: reciprocate 与 reciprocal、reciprocity 同根，语义上与「return」「repay」「exchange」等词相邻。

entries.definition: given or felt by each side towards the other
the practice of exchanging things or favours for mutual benefit
the act of giving or doing something in return
to give back money that was borrowed, or to do something in return for a favour
to give, do, or send back something of the same kind
to give something in return for kindness or harm, now chiefly literary

normalIntro.en: Reciprocate keeps the image of a hand pushing something out and a hand pushing back.
normalIntro.cn: reciprocate 的核心画面是：一只手把东西推出去，另一只手把它推回来。

normal.en: The prefix re- means back, which suits the returning movement inside the word.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「回」，正好对应这个词里折返的动作。

normal.en: Reciprocal and reciprocity are the adjective and noun twins of the same stem.
normal.cn: reciprocal 与 reciprocity 是同一词干的形容词与名词。

normal.en: To reciprocate a kindness is to give kindness back.
normal.cn: reciprocate a kindness 就是把善意还回去。

normal.en: In engineering, a reciprocating engine moves its pistons back and forth.
normal.cn: 工程上，reciprocating engine 指活塞来回运动的往复式发动机。

normal.en: Compare return and repay: reciprocate sounds more formal and stresses that the act mirrors the original one.
normal.cn: 对比 return、repay：reciprocate 更正式，且强调回的那一下与原来那一下对称。

abstract.en: Picture two hands passing a jar of jam back and forth across a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手隔着栅栏把一罐果酱来回传递。

abstract.en: Imagine a smile travelling out and bouncing straight back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个微笑送出去，又笔直地弹回来。

abstract.en: Think of a piston sliding in and out of a cylinder, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象活塞在气缸里一次次滑进又滑出。

examples.en: When a classmate lent him her notes, he reciprocated by helping her with maths.
examples.cn: 同学把笔记借给他，他就帮她补数学作为回报。

examples.en: The service was so good that we felt obliged to reciprocate with a generous tip.
examples.cn: 服务实在太好，我们觉得应该多给一笔小费作为答谢。

examples.en: A reciprocating saw is useful for cutting branches in awkward places.
examples.cn: 往复锯很适合在不好下手的地方锯树枝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞西普若凯特」——瑞西递来一个苹果，普若马上凯特着手回赠一个橘子，正好是「有来有往」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 reciprocus（来回折返；一般认为取「沿原路返回」之意）→ 拉丁语 reciprocare（使折返）→ 英语 reciprocate（回报；往复运动），核心义「一来一回、原路折返」。

sensesIntro.en: Reciprocate starts from a physical back and forth motion, which becomes a returned kindness, a returned feeling, a mechanical stroke, and finally a two sided exchange.
sensesIntro.cn: reciprocate 从物理上的来回折返出发，依次发展为回报善意、回应感情、机械往复，最后是双向的对等交换。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a push that comes straight back along the way it went.
core.cn: 核心意象：推出去的东西沿着原路直直地回来。

branches.en: A favour comes back to the giver as the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 受助者的好意回到施予者身上，这是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Feelings and greetings travel back in the same way as objects.
branches.cn: 情感与寒暄像物品一样原路返回。

branches.en: The piston stroke keeps the literal geometry of the motion.
branches.cn: 活塞冲程保留了这一运动最字面的几何形状。

branches.en: One returned kindness is a gift; equal exchanges on both sides become mutual benefit.
branches.cn: 一次回报是赠礼；双方对等的来回则构成互惠。

branches.en: Diplomats reciprocate greetings and concessions as a two way ritual.
branches.cn: 外交官互相致意、互相让步，把回应变成双向的礼节。

intro.en: Reciprocate is built on the Latin stem reciproco, with the English family reciprocal, reciprocity, and reciprocation around it.
intro.cn: reciprocate 建立在拉丁词干 reciproco 之上，英语中围绕它构成 reciprocal、reciprocity、reciprocation 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin reciprocare means to make something go back, built on reciprocus, moving back and forth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reciprocare 意为「使某物回去」，源于 reciprocus（来回移动的）。

items.example: The re- in reciprocate supports the idea of a return.
items.exampleCN: reciprocate 中的 re- 呼应「返回」之意。

items.example: Reciprocus supplies the back and forth picture.
items.exampleCN: reciprocus 提供来回移动的画面。

items.example: The suffix -ate turns the stem into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把词干变成动词。

items.example: Reciprocate is the core verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: reciprocate 是这个词族的核心动词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms reciprocal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 reciprocal。

items.example: Reciprocal describes a two way relation.
items.exampleCN: reciprocal 描述双向的关系。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms reciprocity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 reciprocity。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms reciprocation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 reciprocation。

items.example: Reciprocation names the returning action.
items.exampleCN: reciprocation 指折返与回报这一行为。

items.example: Reciprocity is the noun of mutual exchange.
items.exampleCN: reciprocity 是「互惠」的名词。

definition_zh: 鲁莽的；不顾后果的；轻率的；不谨慎的；漠视风险的
definition_en: acting or done without thinking about the risks or the possible harm, and without taking care
core_image: 一个人蒙着眼睛在悬崖边走，脚下连看都不看一眼
scene: 暴雨夜里，有人超速闯红灯，车尾灯很快消失在雨幕里。The police fined the young driver for reckless speeding in heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 reckless 是「鲁莽的、不顾后果的」（第 1 个义项：做危险或愚蠢的事却不考虑后果）；句意：警方因这名年轻司机在暴雨中超速鲁莽驾驶而对他处以罚款。

pos.zh: 鲁莽的；不顾后果的；轻率的
不谨慎的；马虎的；漫不经心的

collocations.zh: 毫无顾忌；漠视（法律用语）

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「鲁莽；不顾后果」
形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「鲁莽地；不顾后果地」

senses.title: Acting without counting the cost
senses.definition: doing something dangerous or foolish without thinking about what may go wrong
senses.definitionCN: 做危险或愚蠢的事时完全不考虑可能出什么问题
senses.example: Driving at that speed on a wet road is reckless.
senses.exampleCN: 在湿滑路面上开那么快，是不要命的做法。
senses.why: The word began as reck-less, without reck or care, so a reckless person simply will not stop to count the danger.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本作 reck-less，意思是「不计较、不在意」，所以鲁莽的人根本不肯停下来算一算危险，字面上就是「不核算」。

senses.title: Failing to take proper care
senses.definition: careless in a way that shows too little thought for safety or for other people
senses.definitionCN: 粗心大意到对安全或对他人缺少关心的程度
senses.example: It was reckless of him to leave the stove on all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他让炉子整夜开着，实在太不小心了。
senses.why: The old word reck also meant heed or care, so reck-less shades easily into careless.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 reck 也有「留心、照料」之意，因此由它否定而来的词天然带着「不照料、不留心」的意思。

senses.title: Done with total disregard of risk
senses.definition: showing complete indifference to danger, law, or consequence, as in the legal phrase reckless disregard
senses.definitionCN: 对危险、法律或后果完全无动于衷，法律术语中作「毫无顾忌的漠视」
senses.example: The company showed reckless disregard for safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司对安全规定表现出毫不顾忌的漠视。
senses.why: Law fixes the word into a test of whether a person simply does not care what happens, as if the danger were never entered in the record.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这个词固定成一种判定：当事人对会发生什么毫不在意，仿佛危险从未被登记在案。

intro.en: Reckless is an Old English word: the stem reck, meaning heed or care, with the suffix -less, meaning without.
intro.cn: reckless 是古英语的本土词：词干 reck 意为「留心、在意」，加上表示「没有」的后缀 -less。

items.en: The noun recc carries the sense of care or heed, and the verb reccan means to care about something.
items.cn: 古英语名词 recc 含「关心、留心」之意，动词 reccan 意为「在意某事」。

items.en: Less is added to a stem to mean without, so reckless means literally without care.
items.cn: 古英语在词干后加 -less 表示「没有」，因此 reckless 字面就是「无所顾忌」。

items.en: Reckless is attested from the Old English period, near the ninth and tenth centuries, and early means careless and heedless.
items.cn: reckless 在古英语时期（九至十世纪前后）已有记载，早期意为「粗心、漫不经心」。

items.en: With the growth of the law, the adjective is attached to actions that show no concern for danger or for other people.
items.cn: 随着法律的发展，这个词开始用于形容对危险或他人毫不关心的行为。

items.en: Legal usage fixes phrases such as reckless driving and reckless disregard.
items.cn: 法律用法固定下 reckless driving、reckless disregard 等说法。

items.en: In modern English reckless is the everyday tag for risky action that ignores the cost.
items.cn: 现代英语中 reckless 已成为形容「不顾代价的冒险行为」的常用标签。

note.en: Reckless belongs to the Old English care family, reck, and in meaning sits between careless and the stronger daredevil words.
note.cn: reckless 属于古英语中表示「在意」的词族 reck，语义介于「粗心」与更强烈的「亡命之徒」式词之间。

entries.definition: to care about or take account of, chiefly archaic
not paying enough attention, built with the same -less suffix
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的（同样由 -less 构成，与 reckless 是同一构词法的孪生词）

entries.definition: behaviour that shows no thought for the risks
acting too quickly without thinking enough about what may happen
not taking enough care, often without meaning harm
acting on sudden emotion without stopping to think

normalIntro.en: Reckless is reck plus less: to be reckless is to have no reck, no care at all.
normalIntro.cn: reckless 就是 reck 加 less：不计较、不在意，等于完全不留心。

normal.en: The -less suffix means without, as in careless and hopeless.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 表示「没有」，如 careless、hopeless。

normal.en: Reck is an old word for care or heed, so reckless is simply care without care.
normal.cn: 古英语 reck 意为「在意、留心」，所以 reckless 就是「不在意」。

normal.en: Add -ness for the noun recklessness, and -ly for the adverb recklessly.
normal.cn: 加 -ness 得名词 recklessness，加 -ly 得副词 recklessly。

normal.en: Reckless driving is a standard phrase in traffic law.
normal.cn: reckless driving 是交通法里的固定说法。

normal.en: Compare rash: rash is hasty in the moment, while reckless is a deeper refusal to count the risk.
normal.cn: 对比 rash：rash 是一时的急躁，reckless 则是更根本地不肯去盘算风险。

abstract.en: See a figure on the cliff edge, eyes shut, never looking down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在悬崖边，闭着眼睛，连脚下都不看。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where danger has no column and gets left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账本，危险那一栏干脆空着，什么都不记。

abstract.en: Think of a car whose speedometer is covered with tape.
abstract.cn: 想象车速表被胶带贴住，谁也不知道开了多快。

examples.en: It was reckless of her to lend her savings to a stranger.
examples.cn: 她把积蓄借给陌生人，实在太轻率了。

examples.en: The report accused the company of reckless disregard for public safety.
examples.cn: 报告指责这家公司对公共安全毫不顾忌。

examples.en: Recklessness behind the wheel costs thousands of lives every year.
examples.cn: 驾驶中的鲁莽行为每年夺走成千上万条生命。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞克勒斯」——瑞克开车不留神，把勒斯的车撞了还满不在乎：reckless 就是「不把后果放心上」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 reck/recc（留心、在意）＋ -less（没有）→ reckless（不留心、不顾后果），核心义「事情发生时他根本不放在心上」。

sensesIntro.en: Reckless grows from one small picture: a person who does not care enough to reckon with danger, first in everyday action, then in carelessness, then in the law.
sensesIntro.cn: reckless 从一个很小的画面长出来：一个人懒得盘算危险，先是日常的莽撞，再是马虎不谨慎，最后落到法律的严格用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walking a cliff edge with your eyes tight shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：闭着眼在悬崖边上走。

branches.en: Everyday reckless action ignores the cost of what might go wrong.
branches.cn: 日常语境下的鲁莽行为，等于对可能出现的代价视而不见。

branches.en: Leftover care turns into plain carelessness about safety.
branches.cn: 连基本的照料都不给，就退化成对安全的疏忽。

branches.en: Law makes indifference explicit in the phrase reckless disregard.
branches.cn: 法律用「毫无顾忌」这一表述把漠然写进了条文。

branches.en: A careless slip and a reckless stunt share the same missing care.
branches.cn: 不经心的疏忽与敢于玩命的花招，共享同一份缺失的在意。

branches.en: Ignoring duty carelessly is the everyday face of legal recklessness.
branches.cn: 对职责漫不经心，就是法律意义上鲁莽的日常面目。

intro.en: Reckless is a native Old English word, not a Latin one: the stem reck plus the native suffix -less.
intro.cn: reckless 是古英语本土词，并非拉丁来源：词干 reck 加本土后缀 -less。

latinIntro.en: No Latin parent is needed: the word is native Old English, and only -less has related forms in other Germanic languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不需要拉丁语源头：它出自古英语，只有 -less 在其它日耳曼语中还有同源形式。

items.example: Reck is the living core of the word.
items.exampleCN: reck 是整个词的核心。

items.example: The suffix -less makes reckless mean without care.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 让 reckless 表示「没有在意」。

items.example: Careless uses the very same -less pattern.
items.exampleCN: careless 用的是完全相同的 -less 构词法。

items.example: Hopeless shows the suffix with another stem.
items.exampleCN: hopeless 展示了同一后缀的另一种词干。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms recklessness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 recklessness。

items.example: Recklessness names the state of not caring.
items.exampleCN: recklessness 指不顾后果的状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms recklessly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 recklessly。

items.meaning: in a careless and risky way
items.example: Recklessly describes how a risky act is done.
items.exampleCN: recklessly 描述冒险行为的方式。

items.example: Unrecked is a rare form on the same stem.
items.exampleCN: unrecked 是同一词干上的罕见形式。

definition_zh: 收回；取回；要回（自己的权利）；开垦（荒地）；填海造地；回收利用（废物）；使（土地、水域）恢复原状
definition_en: to get back something that was yours, to bring waste land or waste materials back into use, or to make a degraded place fit for use again
core_image: 一张写着名字的旧契约，被一只手的掌心重新按回桌面
scene: 旧城里那排水渠被填平多年，最近又被挖开、重新流动起来。The city plans to reclaim the abandoned canal and turn it into a walking path.
sceneCN: 这里 reclaim 是「使恢复原状、重新利用」（第 4 个义项：把荒废或受损之地恢复成可用状态）；句意：市政计划把那条废弃的运河重新整理，改造成步道。

pos.zh: 收回；取回；要回
开垦；填海造地；回收利用；使恢复原状

collocations.zh: 重新占用街道；把街区还给居民
领回失物；取回遗失的东西

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「开垦；填海；回收；恢复」
动词加 -able 构成，义为「可收回的；可回收的」
过去分词加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未回收的；未开垦的」
过去分词作定语，义为「回收再用的；已开垦的」

senses.title: To get back what is yours
senses.definition: to get something back that you lost, lent, or were forced to give up
senses.definitionCN: 把丢失、借出或被迫交出的东西拿回来
senses.example: She went to the station to reclaim her lost luggage.
senses.exampleCN: 她去车站领回丢失的行李。
senses.why: The Latin prefix re- puts back and clamer cries out, so reclaim is to call one name out and get the thing back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 re- 表示「回」，clamer 表示「呼喊」，所以 reclaim 就是喊一声「这是我的」，把东西叫回来。

senses.title: To demand back a right
senses.definition: to take back a right, role, or territory that had been taken from you
senses.definitionCN: 重新夺回被剥夺的权利、身份或领土
senses.example: The villagers reclaimed their old fishing rights.
senses.exampleCN: 村民重新要回了他们过去的捕鱼权。
senses.why: A complaint called out in court is the same cry as a name, so reclaim can be a legal demand rather than a physical picking up.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上喊出的诉求与呼喊自己的名字是同一个动作，所以 reclaim 也可以是法律上的主张，而不只是把东西拿在手里。

senses.title: To recover waste material
senses.definition: to process old things such as paper, metal, or rubber so that they can be used again
senses.definitionCN: 处理纸张、金属、橡胶等旧物，使它们能再次被使用
senses.example: The firm reclaims tyres into rubber flooring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把废旧轮胎回收制成橡胶地板。
senses.why: Used material is called back from the rubbish heap into the useful world, so the same cry has a factory side.
senses.whyCN: 废旧材料被从垃圾堆里「叫回」可用世界，于是同一个呼喊的动作生出了工厂里的一面。

senses.title: To bring land or water back to use
senses.definition: to make waste land, swamp, or sea bed fit for building or farming, or to restore a damaged river, canal, or mine
senses.definitionCN: 把荒地、沼泽或海床改造为可供建设或耕种之地，或把受损的河流、运河、矿区恢复原状
senses.example: The project aims to reclaim land from the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目的目标是从海上造地。
senses.why: Falconry gives the oldest technical image: a hawk flown over open ground is called back to the glove, and land called back to use follows the same pattern.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的专门画面其实来自猎鹰：旷野上空飞远的鹰被唤回手套，土地被「唤回」可用状态正好顺着这条路发展。

intro.en: Reclaim comes through Old French from Latin reclamare, to cry out against or call back, built from re- (back) and clamare (to cry out).
intro.cn: reclaim 经古法语来自拉丁语 reclamare（高声反对、唤回），由 re-（回）与 clamare（呼喊）构成。

items.en: Clamare means to cry out, and reclamare means to cry out against or call back. Falconry gives the oldest technical use: a hawk flown over open ground is called back to the glove.
items.cn: clamare 意为「呼喊」，reclamare 意为「高声反对」或「叫回来」；猎鹰术提供了最早的专门用法——在旷野上空飞远的鹰被唤回手套上。

items.en: Reclamer carries both the legal cry, a formal complaint, and the falconer call, fetching a bird back.
items.cn: 古法语 reclamer 兼有法律上的「申诉」与猎鹰术中的「唤回」两层用法。

items.en: The English verb is attested around the end of the fourteenth century, at first for calling back a hawk and for formally demanding a right.
items.cn: 英语动词约在十四世纪末见于记载，起初指唤回猎鹰，也指正式主张权利。

items.en: The sense of getting back something that is yours, and of recovering waste or swamp land, both settle in this period.
items.cn: 「取回属于自己的东西」以及「开垦荒地、沼泽」两义都在这一时期稳定下来。

items.en: Industry gives the word its recycling sense, reclaimed paper and reclaimed rubber, and engineering adds reclaimed water.
items.cn: 工业给了它「回收利用」义，如回收纸、回收橡胶；工程学则带来 reclaimed water（再生水）。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to time, space, and reputation, as in reclaim your time or reclaim the streets.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到时间、空间与名声，如 reclaim your time 或 reclaim the streets。

note.en: Reclaim shares its Latin base clamare with claim, exclaim, and proclaim, and in meaning stands next to recover, restore, and retrieve.
note.cn: reclaim 与 claim、exclaim、proclaim 共有拉丁语基干 clamare，语义上与 recover、restore、retrieve 相邻。

entries.definition: to say something is yours, or to say it is true
to announce something publicly and officially
the process of bringing waste land or material back into use
to find or get back something that was lost
to bring something back to its earlier good condition
to get something back from a place, especially data or an object

normalIntro.en: Reclaim is a shout with a name in it: the prefix re- calls back, and the old root clamer is to cry out.
normalIntro.cn: reclaim 里藏着一句喊名字的话：前缀 re- 表示「回」，古老词干 clamer 表示「呼喊」。

normal.en: Claim is the base word: to reclaim is to claim something back.
normal.cn: 基础词是 claim：reclaim 就是把物权声索回来。

normal.en: Exclaim, proclaim, and acclaim carry the same crying root.
normal.cn: exclaim、proclaim、acclaim 都带着同一个「呼喊」词根。

normal.en: To reclaim land from the sea is to call dry land back out of the water.
normal.cn: reclaim land from the sea 就是把陆地从水里唤回来。

normal.en: Reclaimed wood or water is material called back into use.
normal.cn: reclaimed wood 或 reclaimed water 指被唤回使用中的材料。

normal.en: Reclaim your time means to take back hours that were being drained away.
normal.cn: reclaim your time 指把被耗尽的时间重新夺回。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing an old deed back down on the table to make it count again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张旧地契重新按在桌上，让它重新作数。

abstract.en: See a falcon called down from the sky onto a gloved fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猎鹰被从天上唤回来，落在戴手套的拳头上。

abstract.en: Think of a pile of torn paper going back into a wide clean sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠碎纸重新变成一整张干净的大纸。

examples.en: You can reclaim the tax you paid on the hotel bill.
examples.cn: 你可以退回已付在酒店账单上的税金。

examples.en: The Netherlands has reclaimed large areas of land from the sea.
examples.cn: 荷兰从海里造出了大片土地。

examples.en: She reclaimed her old bike from the shed and repaired it.
examples.cn: 她把旧自行车从棚子里取出来，修好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞克莱姆」——瑞克把克莱姆借他的书要了回来，就是「收回」；不过这纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ clamare（呼喊）→ reclamare（呼喊以反对、唤回）→ 古法语 reclamer → 英语 reclaim（唤回；收回；开垦），核心义「喊一声，把失去的唤回手中」。

sensesIntro.en: Reclaim begins as a legal or falconer cry, and spreads outward: it can call back a lost object, a right, a material, or a piece of land itself.
sensesIntro.cn: reclaim 最初是法庭或猎鹰师的呼喊，随后向外扩散：被唤回的既可以是一件失物，也可以是权利、材料，乃至整片土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a call that brings what went away back into your hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声呼喊，让离开的东西回到自己手里。

branches.en: A lost object answers the call and comes home.
branches.cn: 丢失的东西应声而回，被取回手中。

branches.en: A right answers the call in a legal voice.
branches.cn: 权利以法律的口吻应声，被重新主张。

branches.en: Waste material is called back into the factory.
branches.cn: 废旧材料被唤回工厂继续使用。

branches.en: Objects and rights both come back to the person who claims them.
branches.cn: 物品与权利都回到原主手里，都是物归其主。

branches.en: Industry and engineering both call worn out things back into use.
branches.cn: 工业与工程都在把磨损、荒废之物唤回可用状态。

intro.en: Reclaim is built from the Latin pieces re- and clamer, with the English family claim, exclaim, proclaim, reclamation, and reclaimable.
intro.cn: reclaim 由拉丁成分 re- 与 clamer 构成，英语中围绕它构成 claim、exclaim、proclaim、reclamation、reclaimable 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin clamare, to cry out, gives reclamare, to cry out against or call back; the prefix re- means back again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clamare 意为「呼喊」，由此构成 reclamare（呼喊反对、唤回），前缀 re- 表示「回、再」。

items.example: Re- gives reclaim the idea of bringing back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让 reclaim 含「带回」之意。

items.example: Clamare is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: clamare 是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: to cry out against, to call back
items.example: Reclamare is the direct Latin parent.
items.exampleCN: reclamare 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Claim is the short English twin.
items.exampleCN: claim 是英语中简短的同源词。

items.example: Exclaim keeps the shouting root visible.
items.exampleCN: exclaim 让呼喊的词根一目了然。

items.example: Proclaim adds the idea of speaking out in public.
items.exampleCN: proclaim 加了「当众讲出」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms reclamation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 reclamation。

items.meaning: the act of bringing land or material back into use
items.example: Reclamation names the whole process, not one act.
items.exampleCN: reclamation 指整个过程，而非单一动作。

items.example: The suffix -able forms reclaimable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 reclaimable。

items.meaning: able to be recovered or reused
items.example: Reclaimable describes material that can come back.
items.exampleCN: reclaimable 描述能被回收的材料。

latinEntries.meaning: to cry out against, to call back
one who calls back, a claimant

definition_zh: 认出；辨认；承认；认可；意识到
definition_en: to know someone or something again when you see or hear it, or to accept that something is true or official
core_image: 多年后又看见一张熟悉的脸，眼睛忽然亮了：是它
scene: 街角人群里，她一眼认出了十年前的同桌。In the crowd at the corner she recognised her old deskmate at once.
sceneCN: 这里 recognise 是「认出」（第 1 个义项：再次见到而知悉是谁）；句意：她在街角人群里一眼认出了十年前的同桌。

pos.zh: 认出；辨认出
承认；认可；正式承认

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ion 构成的抽象名词，义为「认出；识别；承认；表彰」
再加 -able 构成，义为「可认出的；可辨认的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「可辨认地；明显地」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未被认出的；未获承认的」

senses.title: To know someone again
senses.definition: to know a person or thing again because you have seen or heard it before
senses.definitionCN: 因为以前见过或听过，而再次知道某人或某物是谁
senses.example: I recognised her voice on the phone at once.
senses.exampleCN: 我在电话里一下就听出了她的声音。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again and cognoscere means to get to know, so the word begins as knowing again.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再一次」，cognoscere 表示「认识、了解」，所以这个词最初的画面就是「再认识一次」。

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept that a fact is true or that a situation exists
senses.definitionCN: 接受某个事实为真，或承认某种情况确实存在
senses.example: She recognised that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: Knowing again can also mean letting a truth back into your mind after resisting it.
senses.whyCN: 「再认识」也可以是把一个曾经抗拒的真相重新接进脑海，于是有了「承认」这一层。

senses.title: To accept as official or valid
senses.definition: to accept a state, government, qualification, or right as official and valid
senses.definitionCN: 把某个国家、政府、资格或权利接受为正式有效
senses.example: The university recognises credits earned abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学认可在国外修得的学分。
senses.why: Official bodies recognise what they choose to see as legitimate, so the perceptual sense of knowing again turns social.
senses.whyCN: 官方机构「认出」什么，就说明它愿意承认什么合法，于是知觉层面的「认出」变成了社会层面的「认可」。

senses.title: To show public appreciation
senses.definition: to give public praise or an award to someone for what they have done
senses.definitionCN: 因某人做了某事而公开表扬或颁奖
senses.example: The council recognised her years of service.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会表彰了她多年的服务。
senses.why: To recognise someone publicly is to make their value visible, as if naming a familiar face in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 公开「认出」某人的价值，就像在人群里点出那张熟悉的脸，于是有了表彰的意思。

intro.en: Recognise goes back to Latin recognoscere, to know again, from re- again and cognoscere, to learn to know.
intro.cn: recognise 上溯拉丁语 recognoscere（再次知道），由 re-（再）与 cognoscere（认识、了解）合成。

items.en: Cognoscere means to get to know, from com- together and gnoscere, to know.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为逐步了解，来自 com-（一起）与 gnoscere（知道）。

items.en: Recognoscere adds re- again and means to know again or to look over.
items.cn: recognoscere 加上 re-（再），意为再次知道或重新审视。

items.en: Reconoistre carries the legal and personal senses of taking notice of a person.
items.cn: 古法语 reconoistre 承接了「注意到某人」的人情与法律含义。

items.en: Recognise enters English meaning to acknowledge and to identify.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，这个词进入英语，意为「承认」与「辨认」。

items.en: Modern English adds computing recognition, and the -ise ending stays standard in British usage.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了计算机「识别」的用法，英式拼写保持 -ise 结尾。

note.en: Recognise belongs to the knowing family of cognoscere, near recognise, cognition, and identify.
note.cn: recognise 属于以 cognoscere 为核心的「知道」词族，与 cognition、identify 等词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of identifying or acknowledging someone
easy to know again
the mental process of knowing
to know or perceive
to establish who or what someone is
entries.definitionCN: 确认某人或某物的身份

entries.definition: to admit or accept that something is true
to agree that something is true, often unwillingly

normalIntro.en: Recognise is to know again: the prefix re- marks the second meeting.
normalIntro.cn: recognise 是「再认识一次」：前缀 re- 标出了第二次相遇。

normal.en: The re- prefix means again, so recognise literally means know again.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再」，所以 recognise 字面就是「再认识」。

normal.en: Recognition is the noun built with -ion.
normal.cn: recognition 是加 -ion 构成的名词。

normal.en: British spelling keeps -ise, while American English writes recognize with z.
normal.cn: 英式拼写用 -ise，美式写作 recognize。

normal.en: To be recognised as means to be generally accepted as.
normal.cn: be recognised as 表示「被普遍认为」。

normal.en: Compare know: know does not imply a second meeting, recognise always does.
normal.cn: 对比 know：know 不含第二次相遇，recognise 一定含。

abstract.en: Picture a face in a crowd suddenly turning into a name.
abstract.cn: 想象人群里一张脸突然变成了一个名字。

abstract.en: Think of a magnifying glass passing slowly over a photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜在照片上慢慢移动，直到找准那一点。

abstract.en: Imagine raising a hand to call out someone who has waited years to be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象你举手点名，叫出一个等了多年的名字。

examples.en: Most people cannot recognise the difference at first glance.
examples.cn: 大多数人一眼无法分辨出差别。

examples.en: The two governments formally recognised each other in that year.
examples.cn: 两国政府在那一年正式相互承认。

examples.en: Doctors are trained to recognise the early signs of the disease.
examples.cn: 医生受过训练，能识别出这种病的早期迹象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞克来的那晚」——一眼就认出了老朋友；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）+ cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再次知道）→ 古法语 reconoistre → 英语 recognise，核心义「再一次知道」。

sensesIntro.en: Recognise starts from seeing a familiar face, then moves to admitting a truth, then to official acceptance, and finally to public honour.
sensesIntro.cn: recognise 从看见熟悉的脸起步，往前是承认真相，再往前是正式认可，最后是公开表彰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar face in a crowd, known again.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群里一张熟悉的脸，被再一次认出来。

branches.en: Knowing a face again is the basic perceptual sense.
branches.cn: 再次认出一张脸是最基本的知觉义。

branches.en: Letting a truth back in is the mental sense of admitting.
branches.cn: 把真相重新放进心里，就是承认这一心理义。

branches.en: An institution that knows something as valid gives official recognition.
branches.cn: 机构「认出」某事有效，就是正式认可。

branches.en: Naming a person before others turns recognition into honour.
branches.cn: 当众点名一个人，认出就变成了表彰。

branches.en: Recognising a fault and admitting it are two steps of the same act.
branches.cn: 看出错误与承认错误是同一动作的两步。

intro.en: Recognise is built on the Latin root gnoscere, to know, wrapped in re- again and the verb ending -ise.
intro.cn: recognise 建在拉丁词根 gnoscere（知道）上，外面套着 re-（再）与动词词尾 -ise。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again, com- means together, and gnoscere means to know.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 表示「再」，com- 表示「一起」，gnoscere 表示「知道」。

items.example: The prefix re- marks a second knowing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标出第二次认识。

items.example: Gnoscere supplies the knowing core.
items.exampleCN: gnoscere 提供「知道」这一核心。

items.example: Cognoscere joins knowing with learning.
items.exampleCN: cognoscere 把「知道」与「了解」合在一起。

items.example: Recognoscere is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: recognoscere 是直接来源。

items.example: The ending -ise forms the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成英语动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms recognition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 recognition。

items.example: The suffix -able forms recognisable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 recognisable。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unrecognised.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unrecognised。

items.example: Cognition shares the knowing root.
items.exampleCN: cognition 共享「知道」词根。

definition_zh: 回忆起；想起；记得
definition_en: to remember something, especially by making an effort to bring it back into your mind
core_image: 弯腰把散落在地上的名字、日期和脸，一件件重新拾起来
scene: 考官问她读过哪些书，她努力回想了一会儿才说出书名。Asked which books she had read, she paused and tried to recollect the titles.
sceneCN: 这里 recollect 是「回忆起」（第 1 个义项：努力从记忆中取回往事）；句意：考官问她读过哪些书，她顿了一下，努力回想书名。

pos.zh: 回忆起；想起
回想；沉思

collocations.phrase: as far as I can recollect

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成的名词，义为「回忆；记忆；回想起来的事情」
过去分词转形容词，义为「镇定自若的；沉思的」（少见）

senses.title: To remember with effort
senses.definition: to bring a past event, name, or detail back into your mind, often by trying hard
senses.definitionCN: 把过去的事、名字或细节重新带进脑海，通常是费力去想
senses.example: I cannot recollect the exact date of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我记不起那次会议的确切日期了。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again and colligere means to gather, so recollecting is gathering facts again from memory.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再」，colligere 表示「收集」，所以回忆就是把散落的记忆再一次收集起来。

senses.title: To recall to calm thought
senses.definition: to take time to gather your thoughts and think quietly about the past
senses.definitionCN: 花一点时间收拢思绪，安静地回想过去
senses.example: He sat by the window and tried to recollect.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐在窗边，努力回想。
senses.why: When the object is omitted the verb becomes an act of gathering yourself, which is quiet reflection.
senses.whyCN: 省略宾语时，这个动词就变成「把自己收拢起来」，于是有了安静沉思的一层。

intro.en: Recollect comes from Latin recolligere, to gather again, from re- again and colligere, to collect.
intro.cn: recollect 来自拉丁语 recolligere（重新收集），由 re-（再）与 colligere（收集）合成。

items.en: Colligere joins com- together and legere to choose or gather, meaning to collect.
items.cn: colligere 由 com-（一起）与 legere（挑选、收集）构成，意为收集。

items.en: Recolligere means to gather again, and later to recover or summon one s mind.
items.cn: recolligere 意为再次收集，后来引申为恢复、收拢心神。

items.en: Recollectio names a gathering together of the mind, and later of memory.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 recollectio 指把心神收拢，再进一步指追忆。

items.en: English recollect takes on the special sense of recalling to memory.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收这个词，逐渐固定为「从记忆中取回」。

items.en: Modern English keeps recollect for effortful remembering, while collect stays concrete.
items.cn: 现代英语仍用 recollect 表示费力想起，而 collect 保持具体的「收集」。

note.en: Recollect is the gathering verb of memory, close to recall, remember, and to the plain verb collect.
note.cn: recollect 是记忆里「收集」的那个动词，与 recall、remember 以及普通的 collect 相邻。

entries.definition: a memory, or the act of remembering
to gather things together
shared by a group
memories shared by a whole group
to bring a fact back to mind
to keep or bring something in mind
to talk or think fondly about the past

normalIntro.en: Recollect is to collect again, so memory work is a small act of tidying up.
normalIntro.cn: recollect 是 collect 加前缀 re-，回忆就是一次小小的重新收拾。

normal.en: The re- prefix means again and lect comes from legere, to gather.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再」，lect 来自 legere（收集）。

normal.en: Recollection is the noun, the things gathered back into memory.
normal.cn: recollection 是名词，指被重新收进记忆里的东西。

normal.en: The phrase with a soft hedge is a common way to talk about memory in court.
normal.cn: 加上一层保留语气的说法，是法庭上谈记忆的常见句式。

normal.en: Collect gathers objects, recollect gathers memories.
normal.cn: collect 收集实物，recollect 收集记忆。

normal.en: Compare remember: remember may happen at once, recollect usually takes effort.
normal.cn: 对比 remember：remember 可以是一下子，recollect 通常要费点力。

abstract.en: Picture picking up scattered photographs and stacking them in order.
abstract.cn: 想象把散落的照片一张张捡起，再按顺序叠好。

abstract.en: Think of a hand drawing a bucket back up out of deep water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把桶从深水里一点点摇上来。

abstract.en: Imagine closing your eyes and walking back down a familiar corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象闭上眼，沿着熟悉的走廊往回走。

examples.en: She could not recollect where she had put the key.
examples.cn: 她想不起来把钥匙放在哪里了。

examples.en: As far as I can recollect, the lecture began at nine.
examples.cn: 据我所能回想的，讲座九点开始。

examples.en: Some students recollect facts better when they write them down.
examples.cn: 有些学生把事实写下来之后回想得更清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + collect」——把散了的东西重新 collect 一遍，就是回想；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）+ colligere（收集）→ recolligere（重新收集）→ 中世纪拉丁语 recollectio（追忆）→ 英语 recollect，核心义「把记忆重新收拢」。

sensesIntro.en: Recollect begins as gathering memory back with effort, and then widens into quiet reflection on the past.
sensesIntro.cn: recollect 先从「费力把记忆收回来」起步，再扩展到安静地回想往事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bending down to pick up scattered memories one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：弯腰把散落的记忆一件件拾起来。

branches.en: Bringing back a name or date is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 想起一个名字或日期，是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Without a clear object, the verb turns into quiet reflection.
branches.cn: 没有明确宾语时，这个动词就变成安静的回想。

branches.en: A person who recollects must first stop and gather the mind.
branches.cn: 回忆的人必须先停下来，把心神收拢。

branches.en: The gathered pieces are what appear later as recollection, the noun of memory.
branches.cn: 收拢起来的碎片，后来就成为名词 recollection 所指的记忆。

branches.en: Slow reflection is the calm cousin of sudden remembering.
branches.cn: 缓慢的回想是突然想起的安静近亲。

intro.en: Recollect is built on Latin legere, to gather or choose, with re- again in front and -ion for the noun.
intro.cn: recollect 建在拉丁语 legere（收集、挑选）上，前面加 re-（再），名词则加 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again, com- means together, and legere means to gather or read.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 表示「再」，com- 表示「一起」，legere 表示「收集」或「读」。

items.example: The prefix re- marks a second gathering.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标出第二次收集。

items.meaning: to gather, to choose, to read
items.example: Legere gives the gathering core to recollect.
items.exampleCN: legere 为 recollect 提供「收集」这一核心。

items.example: Colligere is the family source of collect.
items.exampleCN: colligere 是 collect 一族的来源。

items.example: Recolligere is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: recolligere 是直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms recollection.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 recollection。

items.example: Recollection is the main noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: recollection 是这个词族的主要名词。

items.example: Collect keeps the plain gathering sense.
items.exampleCN: collect 保留朴素的「收集」义。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms collective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 collective。

items.example: Legible shares the reading sense of legere.
items.exampleCN: legible 共享 legere 的「读」义。

latinEntries.meaning: a gathering of the mind, memory

definition_zh: 和解；调解；调和；对账；和谐一致
definition_en: the process of making peace between people who disagreed, or of making two things fit together again
core_image: 两只原本收回的手重新伸出来，握在一起
scene: 两位久不来往的兄弟在父亲的葬礼上终于和解，抱头痛哭。At the funeral of their father, the two estranged brothers finally reached a reconciliation and wept in each other arms.
sceneCN: 这里 reconciliation 是「和解」（第 1 个义项：争执双方重归于好）；句意：在父亲的葬礼上，两位久不来往的兄弟终于和解，抱头痛哭。

pos.zh: 和解；重归于好
调解；调和；对账

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「使和解；使一致；调和」
动词加 -able 构成，义为「可调和的；可协调的」
再加否定前缀 ir- 构成，义为「不可调和的；势不两立的」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「调解者；和事佬」

senses.title: The end of a quarrel
senses.definition: the act of becoming friendly again after a disagreement or quarrel
senses.definitionCN: 在分歧或争吵之后重新变得友好的行为
senses.example: The two families reached a quiet reconciliation.
senses.exampleCN: 两个家庭平静地达成了和解。
senses.why: Latin conciliare means to bring together, and re- means again, so reconciliation is putting people back together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 conciliare 表示「使聚到一起」，re- 表示「再」，所以和解就是把原本散了的人重新凑到一起。

senses.title: The act of making things agree
senses.definition: the act of showing that two ideas, accounts, or sets of facts can both be true
senses.definitionCN: 说明两种说法、账目或事实可以同时成立的行为
senses.example: The report offers a reconciliation of the two accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告给出了两套说法的调和方案。
senses.why: The same bringing together happens in the mind, where two statements must be made to fit.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「凑到一起」也发生在头脑里：两条说法必须彼此对上才能同时成立。

senses.title: The settling of accounts
senses.definition: the accounting process of matching two sets of records so that they agree
senses.definitionCN: 把两套记录核对到一致的对账过程
senses.example: The monthly reconciliation showed a small gap.
senses.exampleCN: 月度对账显示有一处小的差额。
senses.why: Numbers must be reconciled too, and the accountant joins the ledger and the bank statement until they match.
senses.whyCN: 数字也要「和解」：会计把账簿和银行记录拼合起来，直到两边严丝合缝。

senses.title: Peace after conflict
senses.definition: the process of restoring peace and trust in a society divided by conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在因冲突而分裂的社会中恢复和平与信任的过程
senses.example: National reconciliation took more than a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 民族和解花了十多年。
senses.why: When the quarrel is between whole communities, the private act grows into public peacemaking.
senses.whyCN: 当争吵的双方是整个族群时，私人的和解就长成了公共层面的和平建设。

intro.en: Reconciliation comes from Latin reconciliare, to bring together again, from re- again and conciliare, to unite.
intro.cn: reconciliation 来自拉丁语 reconciliare（重新聚合），由 re-（再）与 conciliare（使结合）构成。

items.en: Concilium means an assembly, and conciliare means to bring people together.
items.cn: concilium 意为集会，conciliare 意为使人聚到一起。

items.en: Reconciliare means to restore to favour or friendship.
items.cn: reconciliare 意为恢复好感或友谊。

items.en: Reconciliacion repeats the sense of restoring union.
items.cn: 古法语 reconciliacion 延续了「恢复结合」的含义。

items.en: Medieval Latin uses reconciliatio for restoring peace with God and with others.
items.cn: 中世纪教会拉丁语用 reconciliatio 表示与神、与人和好。

items.en: English reconciliation names both personal peacemaking and the settling of accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收该词，兼指个人的化解与账目的结清。

note.en: Reconciliation is the noun of gather-and-mend, close to its verb reconcile, to the Latin council root, and to settlement words.
note.cn: reconciliation 是「聚合修补」的名词，与动词原形 reconcile、拉丁语「集会」词根以及各类「了结」词相邻。

entries.definition: to make people friendly again, or to make things agree
too opposed to be made to agree
a group that meets to make decisions
advice, or a legal adviser
entries.definitionCN: 建议；法律顾问（与 council 拼写相近，词源相同）

entries.definition: an official agreement ending a dispute
help from a neutral person to settle a dispute
the re-establishing of friendly relations

normalIntro.en: Reconciliation is re plus conciliation: the re- says the joining happens a second time.
normalIntro.cn: reconciliation 是 re 加上 conciliation：「再」字表明这次结合是第二次发生。

normal.en: The verb reconcile drops the -iation and ends in -ile with a long i sound.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 reconcile，去掉名词后缀后重音前移。

normal.en: The Latin concilium assembly gives the council of a group that meets.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 concilium（集会）给出 council 一词，指开会的一群人。

normal.en: To reconcile accounts means to make two records match.
normal.cn: reconcile accounts 就是把两套记录核对到一致。

normal.en: The prefix ir- marks the opposite, as in irreconcilable differences.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 ir- 标出反面，如 irreconcilable differences（不可调和的分歧）。

normal.en: Compare resolve: resolve ends a dispute, reconcile restores the relationship.
normal.cn: 对比 resolve：resolve 是结束争端，reconcile 是恢复关系。

abstract.en: Picture two hands that had been pulled apart stretching back toward each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只被拉开的手重新向对方伸过去。

abstract.en: Think of two torn halves of a page being laid side by side until the lines line up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张撕开两半的纸被并排放好，直到纹路对得上。

abstract.en: Imagine two roads that split in a storm meeting again at a calm junction.
abstract.cn: 想象两条在风暴里分叉的路，在平静的路口重新汇合。

examples.en: A full reconciliation between the neighbours took several years.
examples.cn: 两家邻居彻底和解花了好几年。

examples.en: The company performs a bank reconciliation at the end of each month.
examples.cn: 公司在每月月底做一次银行对账。

examples.en: His memo tried to offer a reconciliation of the two theories.
examples.cn: 他的备忘录用来说明两种理论可以调和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + con + cile」——把两拨人（con）重新（re）攒到一起，就叫和解；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）+ concilium（集会）+ -are（动词）→ reconciliare（重新聚合）→ 教会拉丁语 reconciliatio → 英语 reconciliation，核心义「把人重新凑到一起」。

sensesIntro.en: Reconciliation starts with two people who fell out, then widens to ideas, to ledgers, and to whole nations.
sensesIntro.cn: reconciliation 从闹翻的两个人起步，再扩展到观念、账目，最后到整个民族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands, once withdrawn, reaching out and closing together again.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只原本收回的手重新伸出，握在一起。

branches.en: Two quarrelling people becoming friendly again is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 争执双方重归于好是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Two accounts of the same event being made to agree is the mental sense.
branches.cn: 把对同一事件的两套说法调和一致，是心智层面的义项。

branches.en: A ledger and a bank statement matched line by line is the bookkeeping sense.
branches.cn: 账簿与银行记录逐行对上，是会计层面的义项。

branches.en: A divided nation finding peace is the public form of the same act.
branches.cn: 分裂的民族重获和平，是同一动作的公共形态。

branches.en: Personal forgiveness and national reconciliation share the image of a hand offered again.
branches.cn: 个人原谅与民族和解共享「再次伸出手」的意象。

intro.en: Reconciliation is built on the Latin assembly root concilium, wrapped in re- again and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: reconciliation 建在拉丁语「集会」词根 concilium 上，外面套着 re-（再）与名词后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again, con- means together, and concilium means an assembly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 表示「再」，con- 表示「一起」，concilium 表示「集会」。

items.example: The prefix re- marks a second joining.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标出第二次结合。

items.example: The prefix con- gathers people into one group.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 把人聚成一组。

items.example: Concilium is the assembly image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: concilium 是这个词背后的「集会」意象。

items.example: Conciliare means to bring people into one heart.
items.exampleCN: conciliare 意为把人聚到一条心上。

items.example: Reconciliare is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: reconciliare 是直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms reconciliation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 reconciliation。

items.example: The suffix -able forms reconcilable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 reconcilable。

items.example: The prefix ir- forms irreconcilable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 构成 irreconcilable。

items.example: Council comes straight from concilium.
items.exampleCN: council 直接来自 concilium。

definition_zh: 招聘人员；招工人员；征兵人员；招募者
definition_en: a person or firm whose job is to find and attract new employees, members, or soldiers
core_image: 一个人拿着名册，在场馆里挨个把新名字请进队伍
scene: 招聘会上，招聘方坐在长桌后翻看一摞简历，边看边在名册上圈出人选。At the job fair, the recruiter flipped through a stack of CVs and circled the promising names on the roster.
sceneCN: 这里 recruiter 是「招聘人员」（第 1 个义项：企业里专门物色和吸引新员工的人）；句意：招聘会上，招聘方坐在长桌后翻看一摞简历，边看边在名册上圈出人选。

pos.zh: 招聘人员；招工人员；征兵人员；招募者

derivatives.zh: 招募；招收；征召（动词原形，是 recruiter 的构词基础）
新兵；新成员；新员工（招募来的那个人）
招聘；招募（动词加名词后缀 -ment，指整个过程）
招聘工作；招募活动（现在分词作名词，常作定语）

senses.title: Someone who finds new employees
senses.definition: a person whose job is to look for, test, and hire people for a company
senses.definitionCN: 专职为企业物色、考察并雇用员工的人
senses.example: The recruiter promised to call back within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘人员答应一周内回电。
senses.why: The -er ending makes a doer noun out of recruit, so the word names the person who carries out the hiring.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 把动词 recruit 变成「做事的人」，所以这个词指着「执行招募这个动作的人」。

senses.title: An army recruitment officer
senses.definition: a soldier or officer who persuades young people to join the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 劝年轻人入伍的军人或军官
senses.example: An army recruiter visited the school to talk about careers.
senses.exampleCN: 一位征兵人员来学校介绍职业选择。
senses.why: The original recruiting was of soldiers, so the armed forces sense stays close to the Latin root of growing an army.
senses.whyCN: 最早的招募对象就是士兵，所以「征兵」这层意思最贴近拉丁词根「让军队生长壮大的意思」。

senses.title: A sports talent spotter
senses.definition: a coach or scout who finds talented players and signs them for a team or club
senses.definitionCN: 发现优秀球员并为其球队或俱乐部签约的教练或球探
senses.example: The club sent a recruiter to watch the youth match.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部派了一位人才招募者去看青年队比赛。
senses.why: Teams need bodies as much as armies do, so the same doer noun extends to finding players.
senses.whyCN: 球队和军队一样都缺人手，于是同一个「招募者」名词自然延伸到「找球员」这件事上。

senses.title: A member seeking volunteers
senses.definition: a member of a club, group, or organization whose task is to bring in new people
senses.definitionCN: 负责为俱乐部、团体或组织拉新人的成员
senses.example: As club recruiter, she visits every department each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 作为社团的招募负责人，她每年秋天都去各个院系宣传。
senses.why: Any group that grows needs someone to do the asking, so recruiter also names a member doing the inviting.
senses.whyCN: 任何要壮大的团体都需要有人去开口邀请，所以 recruiter 也指负责拉人的内部成员。

senses.title: A hiring firm or agency
senses.definition: a company or agency that searches for suitable candidates on behalf of employers
senses.definitionCN: 替雇主寻找合适人选的招聘公司或中介机构
senses.example: She was placed by an independent recruiter.
senses.exampleCN: 她是由一家独立招聘机构推荐入职的。
senses.why: The doer suffix can also stand for an institution, once the work is done by an organization rather than one person.
senses.whyCN: 当这项工作由组织而非一个人承担时，「做事者」后缀也会指机构整体。

senses.title: A person who draws others in
senses.definition: a person who brings new people into an activity, cause, or group
senses.definitionCN: 把新人带进某项活动、事业或群体中的人
senses.example: Every charity needs a good recruiter at its core.
senses.exampleCN: 每个慈善机构的核心都需要一位善于拉人的成员。
senses.why: Beyond employment and war, the core action of drawing people in applies to causes and communities as well.
senses.whyCN: 除了雇佣和战争，把人心拉进来的核心动作也可以套用到事业和社群上。

intro.en: Recruiter rests on recruit, which comes from French recruter and is linked to Latin recrescere, to grow again.
intro.cn: recruiter 建在 recruit 之上，recruit 来自法语 recruter，一般认为与拉丁语 recrescere「重新生长」有关。

items.en: Recrescere joins re- again with crescere, to grow.
items.cn: recrescere 由 re-（再）与 crescere（生长）构成。

items.en: The noun recroist or recrue means a new growth, and later new soldiers.
items.cn: 古法语名词 recroist 或 recrue 指新的生长物，后来指新补充的士兵。

items.en: Recruter means to raise new troops to fill up an army.
items.cn: recruter 意为补充新兵以充实军队。

items.en: Recruit enters English as a military noun, then becomes a verb.
items.cn: recruit 先作为军事名词进入英语，随后用作动词。

items.en: Recruiting spreads from armies to schools, clubs, and businesses.
items.cn: 招募从军队扩展到学校、俱乐部与企业。

items.en: Recruiter settles as the person who does the recruiting, with -er as the doer suffix.
items.cn: recruiter 定型为「做招募的人」，其中 -er 是表示做事者的后缀。

note.en: Recruiter belongs to the recruit family and sits near hiring and enlistment words.
note.cn: recruiter 属于 recruit 词族，与招聘、招兵一类的词相邻。

entries.definition: to find and take on new people or soldiers
entries.definitionCN: 招募；招收新成员或新兵（recruiter 的基础形式）

entries.definition: the process of finding and hiring people
entries.definitionCN: 招聘过程；招募行为（recruit 加 -ment）

entries.definition: the activity of attracting new staff or members
entries.definitionCN: 招聘活动（动名词，常作定语）

entries.definition: a person who finds senior staff for other firms
entries.definitionCN: 专门为别的公司物色高级人才的猎头

entries.definition: the person in a company who decides on a hire
entries.definitionCN: 公司里决定聘用谁的用人经理

entries.definition: a person who searches for talented players
entries.definitionCN: 球探；专门发现球员的人

normalIntro.en: Recruiter is recruit plus -er: the recruit action, done by a person.
normalIntro.cn: recruiter 就是 recruit 加 -er：由一个人去做「招募」这件事。

normal.en: The -er suffix marks a doer, as in teacher and builder.
normal.cn: 后缀 -er 表示做事的人，teacher 和 builder 都是这样。

normal.en: Recruit shares a Latin root with crescent, both suggesting growth.
normal.cn: recruit 与 crescent 共享拉丁词根，都含「生长」之意。

normal.en: A recruiter grows a team the way a plant grows new shoots.
normal.cn: 招聘人员让团队壮大，就像植物长出新的枝条。

normal.en: Recruitment is the process, recruiter is the person.
normal.cn: recruitment 是过程，recruiter 是人。

normal.en: An army recruiter and a job recruiter both sign people up.
normal.cn: 征兵的老兵招募官和企业招聘人员，都在让人「入伙」。

abstract.en: Picture a long table with a name list and a pen circling candidates.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，一张名册，一支笔在上面圈出人选。

abstract.en: Imagine a tent with a flag, where new soldiers queue to sign their names.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶插旗的帐篷，新兵排队在上面签名。

abstract.en: See a scout in the stands quietly jotting down a player number.
abstract.cn: 想象看台上一位球探悄悄记下一个球衣号码。

examples.en: The recruiter asked her why she wanted to work in finance.
examples.cn: 招聘人员问她为什么想从事金融行业。

examples.en: A recruiter from the university visits our campus every spring.
examples.cn: 大学的招生宣传负责人每年春天都会来我们校园。

examples.en: Good firms often hire recruiters before they post a vacancy.
examples.cn: 好公司常常在发布职位之前先请好招聘人员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞克如特」——像在会场到处问「你愿意来吗」，把人一个个请进队伍；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）+ crescere（生长）→ 一般认为与 recrescere（重新生长）同源 → 法语 recruter（补充新兵）→ 英语 recruit（招募）→ recruit + -er（做事者）→ recruiter，核心义「让队伍重新长出新人」。

sensesIntro.en: Recruiter starts with the person who hires staff, then extends to army and sports finding, group membership, and finally an agency.
sensesIntro.cn: recruiter 先指为企业招人的人，随后延伸到征兵、体育选材、团体拉新，最后指招聘机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a roster inviting new names into a group.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着名册，把新名字请进队伍。

branches.en: The workplace hiring sense is the most common modern use.
branches.cn: 职场招聘是现代最常见的一层。

branches.en: The army sense keeps the oldest layer of meaning.
branches.cn: 征兵义保留着最古老的「补充兵员」含义。

branches.en: Sports recruitment borrows the same need to fill a team.
branches.cn: 体育招募借用了同样的「补人上位」需求。

branches.en: Both a company recruiter and a club recruiter ask people to join.
branches.cn: 企业招聘人员和社团招募负责人，本质都在请人加入。

branches.en: An agency and an individual can both carry the recruiting role.
branches.cn: 机构和个人都可以承担招募这一角色。

intro.en: Recruiter is built from the verb recruit, the re- prefix, the Latin root crescere, and the doer suffix -er.
intro.cn: recruiter 由动词 recruit、前缀 re-、拉丁词根 crescere 与做事者后缀 -er 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again and crescere means to grow, combining in the notion of growing troops again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 意为「再」，crescere 意为「生长」，合起来是「让队伍重新生长」。

items.example: The prefix re- means again.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再」。

items.example: Crescere gives the growing image.
items.exampleCN: crescere 提供「生长」的意象。

items.example: Recrescere joins re- with crescere.
items.exampleCN: recrescere 由 re- 与 crescere 组成。

items.example: French recruter carries the military sense.
items.exampleCN: 法语 recruter 承载了军事含义。

items.example: Recruit is the English base verb.
items.exampleCN: recruit 是英语的基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms recruiter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 recruiter。

items.example: Recruiter names the doing person.
items.exampleCN: recruiter 指执行招募的人。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms recruitment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 recruitment。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms process nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成表示过程的名词。

definition_zh: 恢复健康；康复；休养；挽回（损失）
definition_en: to get back your health, strength, or money after illness, hard work, or loss
core_image: 病床上的人一点点重新攒回力气，重新坐起来
scene: 手术后，老人每天在花园里慢慢走几圈，把力气一点点攒回来。After the operation the old man took a short walk in the garden daily and slowly recuperated his strength.
sceneCN: 这里 recuperate 是「恢复体力」（第 1 个义项：生病或劳累后重新获得健康与体力）；句意：手术后，老人每天在花园里慢慢走几圈，把力气一点点攒回来。

pos.zh: 康复；恢复健康；休养
恢复（健康、体力）；挽回（损失）

derivatives.zh: 康复；恢复（动词加名词后缀 -ation，指整个恢复过程）
有助于康复的；恢复性的（加形容词后缀 -ive）
可恢复的；可挽回的（加 -able 表示「能……的」）
恢复能力（recuperative 作定语与 capacity 组合的常用说法）

senses.title: To get your health back
senses.definition: to become well and strong again after an illness or injury
senses.definitionCN: 在生病或受伤之后重新变得健康、有力
senses.example: It took her three months to recuperate after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后她花了三个月才康复。
senses.why: The Latin root names getting back what was taken, and health is the thing most visibly taken by illness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根的本义是「把被拿走的东西拿回来」，而疾病拿走的最明显的东西正是健康。

senses.title: To rest until strong again
senses.definition: to spend a period resting or being cared for so that strength returns
senses.definitionCN: 花一段时间休息或接受照料，使体力重新回来
senses.example: He is recuperating in the countryside for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他这个夏天在乡下休养。
senses.why: Because health comes back over time, the verb also names the waiting and resting period itself.
senses.whyCN: 健康需要时间才能回来，所以这个动词也指「慢慢养」的这段过程。

senses.title: To regain strength or energy
senses.definition: to recover the energy or powers used up by hard work or effort
senses.definitionCN: 把因劳累或用力而消耗的体力和精力补回来
senses.example: The team needs a week to recuperate before the next match.
senses.exampleCN: 球队需要一周时间恢复体力，才能迎接下一场比赛。
senses.why: Strength spent is like money spent, so the same getting back applies to energy and power.
senses.whyCN: 耗掉的体力就像花掉的钱，同样可以用「把花掉的东西补回来」的动作来理解。

senses.title: To win back a lost position
senses.definition: to regain a position or advantage that had been lost in competition
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争中重新拿回先前失去的位置或优势
senses.example: The firm hopes to recuperate lost market share.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司希望能挽回失去的市场份额。
senses.why: Outside medicine, the thing taken away can be a market position, so the verb extends to winning it back.
senses.whyCN: 在医学之外，被拿走的东西也可以是市场地位，于是动词延伸到「把它夺回来」。

senses.title: To recover money or losses
senses.definition: to get back money that was lost or spent, or to make up for a loss
senses.definitionCN: 收回失去或花掉的钱，或弥补损失
senses.example: The insurer hoped to recuperate part of the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司希望能收回一部分成本。
senses.why: This is the most literal use: the object taken away is money, and it is brought back.
senses.whyCN: 这是最本义的用法：被拿走的对象就是钱，而钱又被拿回来。

intro.en: Recuperate comes from Latin recuperare, to get back or regain, built on capere, to take, with a re- form.
intro.cn: recuperate 来自拉丁语 recuperare（取回、重新获得），以 capere（拿取）为词根，前面带 re- 的形式。

items.en: Recuperare means to get back, recover, or regain.
items.cn: recuperare 意为取回、恢复、重新获得。

items.en: It is linked to capere, to take, so to recuperate is to seize back.
items.cn: 它与 capere（拿取）相关，所以 recuperare 的本义是「再夺回来」。

items.en: Recuperatio names recovery, especially of goods or property.
items.cn: recuperatio 指恢复，尤指财物或产业的取回。

items.en: Recuperate enters English with the sense of getting back something lost.
items.cn: recuperate 进入英语时意为「取回失去之物」。

items.en: The medical sense of regaining health becomes the dominant one.
items.cn: 「恢复健康」这一医学含义逐渐成为主流。

items.en: Recuperation now covers health, energy, money, and lost positions.
items.cn: 现代的 recuperation 涵盖健康、体力、金钱与失去的位置。

note.en: Recuperate shares the capere root family and sits next to words about recovering and healing.
note.cn: recuperate 与 capere 词根家族同源，并与「恢复、治愈」一类词相邻。

entries.definition: the process of getting health or strength back
entries.definitionCN: 康复过程（recuperate 加 -ation 的名词形式）

entries.definition: helping someone to recover
entries.definitionCN: 有助于康复的；恢复性的

entries.definition: to become well again or get something back
entries.definitionCN: 恢复；找回（拼写与意义都接近，但词根源自不同拉丁词，只是相近）

entries.definition: to spend time getting well after an illness
to stop working so that you feel stronger
to make a wound or injury healthy again

normalIntro.en: Recuperate is Latin recuperare, to seize back, with the capere family behind it.
normalIntro.cn: recuperate 来自拉丁语 recuperare（再夺回来），背后是 capere 家族。

normal.en: Recuperation is the noun, recuperative the adjective.
normal.cn: recuperation 是名词，recuperative 是形容词。

normal.en: Convalesce is the common near-synonym for recovering slowly.
normal.cn: convalesce 是「慢慢康复」的常用近义词。

normal.en: To recuperate money is to get money back.
normal.cn: recuperate money 就是把钱收回来。

normal.en: The capere root also lies behind capture.
normal.cn: capere 这个词根也演变成 capture。

normal.en: Hospitals and rest homes are built for recuperation.
normal.cn: 医院和休养所正是为 recuperation 而建的。

abstract.en: Picture a cat on a windowsill slowly regaining its strength.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫趴在窗台上，力气一点点回来。

abstract.en: Think of a battery recharging from red back to green.
abstract.cn: 想象一块电池从红色指针慢慢回绿。

abstract.en: Imagine a fisherman pulling a net back out of the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象渔夫把网从海里重新拉回来。

examples.en: She went to the coast to recuperate after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术之后她到海边去休养。

examples.en: Patients need quiet rooms in order to recuperate properly.
examples.cn: 病人需要安静的房间才能好好康复。

examples.en: By the second half the runners had recuperated their energy.
examples.cn: 到了下半场，跑步的选手们已经恢复了体力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「日 K 频累特」——每天累得只想躺下，躺够了才慢慢缓过来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）+ 词根 cuper / capere（拿取）→ recuperare（取回、重新获得）→ 晚期拉丁语 recuperare → 英语 recuperate / recuperation，核心义「把失去的东西重新抓回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Recuperate begins with getting health back, then resting, then renewing energy, and finally winning back a position or money.
sensesIntro.cn: recuperate 从「重新获得健康」开始，进而指休养、恢复体力，最后指夺回位置或收回钱款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weakened person slowly standing up again.
core.cn: 核心意象：虚弱的人一点点重新站起来。

branches.en: Getting health back is the central medical sense.
branches.cn: 重新获得健康是核心的医学义项。

branches.en: Slow recovery turns the verb into the act of resting.
branches.cn: 缓慢的恢复让动词转而指「休养」这种行为。

branches.en: Energy and strength work like money that can be won back.
branches.cn: 体力和精力就像可以赢回来的钱。

branches.en: Position and money are the non-medical uses of the same getting back.
branches.cn: 位置与金钱是同一个「取回」动作的非医学用法。

branches.en: Health, rest, and energy form one continuous recovery story.
branches.cn: 健康、休养与体力构成一条连续的康复故事。

intro.en: Recuperate is re- plus the capere take root, and English adds -ation, -ative, and -able around it.
intro.cn: recuperate 由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成，英语围绕它构成 -ation、-ative、-able 等形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again and capere means to take, giving recuperare, to take back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 意为「再」，capere 意为「拿」，合起来是「再拿回来」。

items.example: The prefix re- signals doing again.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示再做一次。

items.example: Capere lies behind capture.
items.exampleCN: capere 演变成 capture。

items.example: Recuperare gives the English verb.
items.exampleCN: recuperare 提供英语动词的来源。

items.example: Recuperatio names the recovery.
items.exampleCN: recuperatio 表示恢复。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms verbs.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成动词。

items.example: Recuperate is the English verb.
items.exampleCN: recuperate 是英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms recuperation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 recuperation。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms recuperative.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 recuperative。

items.example: The suffix -able forms recuperable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 recuperable。

items.example: Recuperation names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: recuperation 指整个恢复过程。

definition_zh: 回收利用；再循环；重新使用；废物利用
definition_en: to treat used materials so that they can be used again, or to use something again
core_image: 三个箭头首尾相接，转成一个找不出起点的圆环
scene: 厨房里有两只桶，一只是厨余，一只是被压扁的纸盒和瓶子。In the kitchen there are two bins, one for food waste and one for flattened cartons and bottles to recycle.
sceneCN: 这里 recycle 是「回收利用」（第 1 个义项：把用过的材料处理后再投入使用）；句意：厨房里有两只桶，一只是厨余，一只是压扁的纸盒和瓶子，准备回收。

pos.zh: 回收利用；重新使用
可回收；实行回收
再循环（尤指计算机上删除后仍可在回收站找回）

derivatives.zh: 回收利用；再利用（动词加 -ing 作名词，指整个过程）
可回收利用的（加 -able 表示「可以被……的」）
回收者；回收设备（加表示做事者的 -er）
回收站；回收箱（recycle 作定语与 bin 组合的常用说法）

senses.title: To treat waste so it can be used again
senses.definition: to treat paper, glass, plastic, or metal so that it can be made into new things
senses.definitionCN: 处理纸、玻璃、塑料或金属，使它们能被制成新东西
senses.example: We recycle glass bottles at the corner of the street.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在街角回收玻璃瓶。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again and cycle means a circle, so the word names sending a used material round the circle once more.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再」，词根 cycle 表示「圆圈」，合起来就是把用过的材料再绕一圈送回起点。

senses.title: To use something again for a new purpose
senses.definition: to find a new use for something already used, without treating it chemically
senses.definitionCN: 不经过化学处理，直接为一度用过的东西找到新用途
senses.example: She recycles old jars as pen holders.
senses.exampleCN: 她把旧玻璃罐改作笔筒。
senses.why: Even without a factory, the idea of putting an object back into circulation fits the same circle of use.
senses.whyCN: 即使不经工厂，把物品重新放回使用流程，也符合同一个「循环」意象。

senses.title: For a material to be recyclable
senses.definition: of a material, to be able to go through processing and be used again
senses.definitionCN: 就材料而言，能够经过处理后被再次使用
senses.example: Thin plastic films are hard to recycle.
senses.exampleCN: 薄塑料膜很难回收。
senses.why: As an intransitive verb, the subject is the material itself, which can or cannot go round the circle.
senses.whyCN: 作不及物动词时，主语就是材料本身，它能不能绕完这一圈决定了能否回收。

senses.title: To take rubbish for reprocessing
senses.definition: to collect household or industrial waste for reprocessing, as a policy or practice
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种政策或习惯，收集生活垃圾或工业废物以供再加工
senses.example: The city now recycles nearly half of its household waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市现在能回收近一半的生活垃圾。
senses.why: When a whole city collects and processes waste, the object widens from one bottle to the entire stream.
senses.whyCN: 当整座城市都在收集和处理垃圾时，动作对象就从一只瓶子扩大到整个废物流。

senses.title: To bring back deleted files
senses.titleCN: 恢复（被删除的文件）；清空回收站
senses.definition: in computing, to move deleted files back, or to empty a temporary holding area
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机中把删除的文件移回原处，或清空存放这些文件的临时区域
senses.example: Click here to recycle the deleted files.
senses.exampleCN: 点击这里把已删除的文件移入回收站。
senses.why: The circle image turns digital: a deleted file can go round once more instead of being destroyed.
senses.whyCN: 圆形意象在数字世界再次生效：被删除的文件也可以再绕一圈，而不是彻底消失。

senses.title: To take part in recycling
senses.definition: of people, to sort waste and put recyclable things into the right container
senses.definitionCN: 就人而言，把垃圾分类，把可回收的东西投进正确的容器
senses.example: Families here recycle more than they throw away.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的人家回收的东西比扔掉的多。
senses.why: The user becomes the subject, and the verb names the habit of keeping materials in the circle.
senses.whyCN: 当使用者成为主语时，这个动词指的就是「让材料留在循环里」的日常习惯。

intro.en: Recycle is a modern English coinage, made of Latin re- again and the Greek-derived cycle, a circle.
intro.cn: recycle 是现代英语新造的词，由拉丁语 re-（再）与源自希腊语的 cycle（圆圈）组成。

items.en: Kyklos means circle or wheel.
items.cn: kyklos 意为圆圈或车轮。

items.en: Re- means again or back.
items.cn: re- 意为「再」或「回」。

items.en: Cycle enters English as a noun for a recurring round of events.
items.cn: cycle 作为名词进入英语，指周而复始的一轮。

items.en: Cycle varies to mean a bicycle and later to move in a circle.
items.cn: cycle 又衍生出自行车之意，后来又指「循环运转」。

items.en: Recycle is coined in the nineteen twenties for reusing oil and later paper.
items.cn: recycle 在二十世纪二十年代被造出来，起初指油的再利用，后来扩展到纸张。

items.en: Recycling grows into a household word with the environmental movement.
items.cn: 随着环保运动兴起，recycling 成为家喻户晓的词。

note.en: Recycle contains cycle and re-, and sits near words about reusing and reducing waste.
note.cn: recycle 含有 cycle 与 re-，与「再利用、减少废物」一类词相邻。

entries.definition: the process of treating waste for reuse
entries.definitionCN: 回收利用的过程（recycle 的现在分词或名词形式）

entries.definition: able to be recycled
a repeated series of events or a bicycle
entries.definitionCN: 循环；周期；自行车（recycle 的核心词根）

entries.definition: to use something again instead of throwing it away
to give an old object a new purpose
to save usable parts from waste or damage
entries.definitionCN: 抢救；从废物中回收有用之物

normalIntro.en: Recycle is re- plus cycle, sending a material round the circle one more time.
normalIntro.cn: recycle 就是 re- 加 cycle，让材料沿着圆圈再走一圈。

normal.en: Re- means again, as in rebuild and rewrite.
normal.cn: re- 表示「再」，rebuild 和 rewrite 都是这样。

normal.en: Recycling is the noun, recyclable the adjective.
normal.cn: recycling 是名词，recyclable 是形容词。

normal.en: A recycling bin is where the circle begins again.
normal.cn: 回收桶就是这个圆重新开始的地方。

normal.en: Recycled paper closes the loop between library and mill.
normal.cn: 再生纸让图书馆与造纸厂之间的回路闭合。

normal.en: Compare reuse: reuse skips the factory, recycle goes through it.
normal.cn: 对比 reuse：重复使用跳过工厂，回收利用要经过工厂。

abstract.en: Picture three arrows chasing each other in a green ring.
abstract.cn: 想象三个箭头在绿色圆环里互相追赶。

abstract.en: Imagine a used bottle sailing back across the sea to a new life.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用过的瓶子漂回海上，开启新的生命。

abstract.en: Think of a squeezed can that pops open into a new one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被压扁的铝罐重新鼓起来，变成新的罐子。

examples.en: Our school recycles paper and plastic every week.
examples.cn: 我们学校每周回收纸张和塑料。

examples.en: Recycled glass needs much less energy than new glass.
examples.cn: 再生玻璃所需的能源远少于新玻璃。

examples.en: Households now sort their rubbish so that it can be recycled.
examples.cn: 现在家庭会把垃圾分类，以便回收利用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「日赛狗」——一只狗绕着院子一圈圈地转，转完还会回到起点；这圈就是 recycling 的形状。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再、回）+ 希腊语 kyklos（圆圈）→ 英语 cycle（循环；一圈）→ re + cycle → recycle，核心义「让用过的材料再绕一圈回到起点」。

sensesIntro.en: Recycle starts with processing waste for reuse, then reusing objects, being recyclable, city-level collection, computing, and personal habits.
sensesIntro.cn: recycle 先指处理废物再利用，再指把旧物改作他用、材料可回收、城市层面收集废物、计算机操作以及个人参与回收。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three arrows forming a closed green loop.
core.cn: 核心意象：三个箭头首尾相接，围成一个闭合的绿色环。

branches.en: Industrial processing of waste is the central sense.
branches.cn: 工厂处理废物是核心义项。

branches.en: Personal reuse is the same loop without a factory.
branches.cn: 个人改造再利用，就是没有工厂的同一个循环。

branches.en: Materials that can survive the loop are recyclable.
branches.cn: 能撑过这一圈的材料就是可回收的。

branches.en: Cities and individuals act at the two ends of collection.
branches.cn: 城市与个人分别处在收集环节的两端。

branches.en: Deleted files go round the digital loop instead of dying.
branches.cn: 被删除的文件走的是数字回路，而不是直接消失。

intro.en: Recycle joins Latin re- with the Greek-derived cycle, and English builds recycling, recyclable, and recycler on it.
intro.cn: recycle 由拉丁语 re- 与源自希腊语的 cycle 组合而成，英语又围绕它构成 recycling、recyclable 与 recycler。

latinIntro.en: The re- prefix means again, and cycle comes from Greek kyklos, a circle or wheel.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 意为「再」，cycle 来自希腊语 kyklos，意为圆圈或车轮。

items.example: The prefix re- means once more.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示再一次。

items.example: Kyklos gives the circle image.
items.exampleCN: kyklos 提供圆圈意象。

items.meaningCN: 小事物（与 cycle 的词形演变有关）
items.example: Cycle carries the small circle form.
items.exampleCN: cycle 保留了小圆圈的形式。

items.example: Cycle is the core of the word.
items.exampleCN: cycle 是本词的核心。

items.example: Recycle is the modern compound.
items.exampleCN: recycle 是现代复合词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms recycling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 recycling。

items.example: The suffix -able forms recyclable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 recyclable。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms recycler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 recycler。

items.example: Recycling names the whole loop.
items.exampleCN: recycling 指整个循环过程。

items.example: Recyclable marks the material.
items.exampleCN: recyclable 描述材料。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 圆圈（希腊语 kyklos 的拉丁化形式）

definition_zh: 重新开发；重建改造；（经济或城市的）更新振兴
definition_en: the process of developing an area, a building, or an economy again, especially after it has become old or run down
core_image: 推土机推倒旧街区，随后竖起高楼和绿色广场
scene: 老城区被拆掉重建。The old harbour district is being rebuilt in a large redevelopment.
sceneCN: 这里 redevelopment 是「重新开发、重建改造」（第 1 个义项：对旧城区或旧建筑进行再次开发建设）；句意：旧港口区正在大规模重建中。

pos.zh: 重新开发；重建改造

derivatives.zh: 重新开发；改造：re-（再）+ develop（发展）
重建者；改造开发商：redevelop + -er
发展；开发：名词去掉前缀 re- 后的基础动词
发展；开发：develop + -ment，是重新开发的基础名词
开发商：develop + -er，指动手建设的一方

senses.title: Rebuilding an area or a building
senses.definition: the process of pulling down or restructuring old buildings and building again on the same site
senses.definitionCN: 拆掉或改造旧建筑、在同一地块上重新建设的过程
senses.example: The docklands redevelopment brought new housing along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 码头区的改造让河边多了一片新住宅。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again, so the word begins from the core image of taking a site back to before development and starting over.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再一次」，所以这个词从核心意象出发：先让地块回到「尚未开发」的状态，再重新建起。

senses.title: A renewal scheme with a plan
senses.definition: a planned scheme, often backed by public money, for renewing a district designated as run down
senses.definitionCN: 通常由政府资金支持、针对被认定衰败的区域制定的更新工程
senses.example: The council approved a city-centre redevelopment worth millions.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会批准了一项价值数百万的市中心改造计划。
senses.why: Once rebuilding becomes public policy, the word names the whole scheme rather than one building, so the image of a demolished block becomes a map full of redrawn plots.
senses.whyCN: 当重建上升为公共政策时，这个词就不再指一栋楼，而指整套工程；核心意象里被推倒的街区，也就变成了一张划满新地块的地图。

senses.title: Economic rebuilding
senses.definition: the effort to revive an economy, industry, or region that has declined
senses.definitionCN: 振兴衰退的经济、产业或地区的努力
senses.example: Coal regions depend on redevelopment to attract new industry.
senses.exampleCN: 煤炭产区依靠产业再开发来吸引新工业。
senses.why: The rebuilding image moves from land to livelihoods; what is torn down is an outdated industry and what rises in its place is a new one.
senses.whyCN: 重建的画面从土地扩展到生计：拆掉的是过时的产业，顶上来的是一套新的产业。

senses.title: The work of giving a place new features
senses.definition: the work of giving an existing place new functions such as shops, parks, or offices
senses.definitionCN: 为已有的地方增添商店、公园、办公楼等新用途的工程
senses.example: The station redevelopment added a market and a roof garden.
senses.exampleCN: 车站的改造新增了市场和屋顶花园。
senses.why: Development can mean adding something new to what exists, so redevelopment sometimes keeps the old shell and changes what happens inside it.
senses.whyCN: development 也可以指在原有基础之上增添新内容，所以 redevelopment 有时保留旧外壳，只改变里面发生的事情。

intro.en: Redevelopment is the word develop with the Latin prefix re- added, then carried into a noun by the suffix -ment.
intro.cn: redevelopment 是 develop 加上拉丁语前缀 re- 之后，再由后缀 -ment 构成的名词。
